# FSharp.Core

## Docs

### [F# Core Library Documentation](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/index.md)

F# Core Library Documentation
This site contains the documentation for the FSharp.Core library used in all F# code.
FSharp.Core contains functionality for basic F# definitions, operations for collections such as lists, maps and sequences,
and library functionality for quotations, reflections, events, asynchronous programming and native interoperability.
The following namespaces are available:

FSharp.Core - Basic definitions of options, functions, operators, results and formatting.
FSharp.Collections - Operations for collections such as lists, arrays, sets, maps and sequences. See also F# Collection Types in the F# Language Guide.
FSharp.Control - Library functionality for asynchronous programming, events and agents. See also F# Asynchronous Programming in the F# Language Guide.
FSharp.Linq - Library functionality for F# query syntax and interoperability with .NET Expressions. See also F# Query Expressions in the F# Language Guide.
FSharp.Quotations - Library functionality for F# quotations. See also F# Code Quotations in the F# Language Guide.
FSharp.Reflection - Library functionality for accessing additional information about F# types and F# values at runtime, augmenting that available through System.Reflection. See also F# Reflection in the F# Wiki Book.
FSharp.NativeInterop - Basic functionality for native interopability. See also F# External Functions in the F# Language Guide.
FSharp.Core.CompilerServices - Library functionality for supporting type providers and code generated by the F# compiler. See also F# Type Providers in the F# Language Guide.

Contributing to this documentation
To contribute to this documentation site and its content, please see the notes in the corresponding GitHub repository.

### [Array.allPairs](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#allPairs)

Array.allPairs 
allPairs 
Returns a new array that contains all pairings of elements from the first and second arrays. 
This is an O(n*m) operation, where n and m are the lengths of the arrays.

### [Array.append](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#append)

Array.append 
append 
Builds a new array that contains the elements of the first array followed by the elements of the second array. 
This is an O(n+m) operation, where n and m are the lengths of the arrays.

### [Array.average](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#average)

Array.average 
average 
Returns the average of the elements in the array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.averageBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#averageBy)

Array.averageBy 
averageBy 
Returns the average of the elements generated by applying the function to each element of the array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.blit](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#blit)

Array.blit 
blit 
Reads a range of elements from the first array and write them into the second. 

 Slicing syntax is generally preferred, e.g.
 <pre class="fssnip highlighted"><code lang="fsharp"> <span class="k">let</span> <span data-fsdocs-tip="fs1" data-fsdocs-tip-unique="1" class="id">source</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="pn">[|</span> <span class="n">12</span><span class="pn">;</span> <span class="n">13</span><span class="pn">;</span> <span class="n">14</span> <span class="pn">|]</span>
 <span class="k">let</span> <span data-fsdocs-tip="fs2" data-fsdocs-tip-unique="2" class="id">target</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="pn">[|</span> <span class="n">0</span><span class="pn">;</span> <span class="n">1</span><span class="pn">;</span> <span class="n">2</span><span class="pn">;</span> <span class="n">3</span><span class="pn">;</span> <span class="n">4</span><span class="pn">;</span> <span class="n">5</span> <span class="pn">|]</span>
 <span data-fsdocs-tip="fs2" data-fsdocs-tip-unique="3" class="id">target</span><span class="pn">[</span><span class="n">3..</span><span class="n">4</span><span class="pn">]</span> <span class="k"><-</span> <span data-fsdocs-tip="fs1" data-fsdocs-tip-unique="4" class="id">source</span><span class="pn">[</span><span class="n">1..</span><span class="n">2</span><span class="pn">]</span>
</code></pre>
<div popover class="fsdocs-tip" id="fs1">val source: int array</div>
<div popover class="fsdocs-tip" id="fs2">val target: int array</div>


  This is an O(count) operation.

### [Array.collect](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#collect)

Array.collect 
collect 
For each element of the array, applies the given function. Concatenates all the results and return the combined array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the total output length.

### [Array.compareWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#compareWith)

Array.compareWith 
compareWith 
Compares two arrays using the given comparison function, element by element. 
This is an O(min(n,m)) operation, where n and m are the lengths of the arrays.

### [Array.concat](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#concat)

Array.concat 
concat 
Builds a new array that contains the elements of each of the given sequence of arrays. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the total number of elements across all arrays.

### [Array.contains](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#contains)

Array.contains 
contains 
Tests if the array contains the specified element. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.copy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#copy)

Array.copy 
copy 
Builds a new array that contains the elements of the given array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.countBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#countBy)

Array.countBy 
countBy 
Applies a key-generating function to each element of an array and returns an array yielding unique
 keys and their number of occurrences in the original array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.create](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#create)

Array.create 
create 
Creates an array whose elements are all initially the given value. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the count.

### [Array.tryHead](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#tryHead)

Array.tryHead 
tryHead 
Returns the first element of the array, or
 <code>None</code> if the array is empty. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.tryPick](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#tryPick)

Array.tryPick 
tryPick 
Applies the given function to successive elements, returning the first
 result where the function returns <code>Some(x)</code> for some <code>x</code>. If the function
 never returns <code>Some(x)</code> then <code>None</code> is returned. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.fill](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#fill)

Array.fill 
fill 
Fills a range of elements of the array with the given value. 
This is an O(count) operation.

### [Array.pick](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#pick)

Array.pick 
pick 
Applies the given function to successive elements, returning the first
 result where the function returns <code>Some(x)</code> for some <code>x</code>. If the function
 never returns <code>Some(x)</code> then <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.keynotfoundexception">KeyNotFoundException</a> is raised. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.choose](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#choose)

Array.choose 
choose 
Applies the given function to each element of the array. Returns
 the array comprised of the results <code>x</code> for each element where
 the function returns <code>Some(x)</code> 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.chunkBySize](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#chunkBySize)

Array.chunkBySize 
chunkBySize 
Divides the input array into chunks of size at most <code>chunkSize</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.distinct](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#distinct)

Array.distinct 
distinct 
Returns an array that contains no duplicate entries according to generic hash and
 equality comparisons on the entries.
 If an element occurs multiple times in the array then the later occurrences are discarded. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.distinctBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#distinctBy)

Array.distinctBy 
distinctBy 
Returns an array that contains no duplicate entries according to the
 generic hash and equality comparisons on the keys returned by the given key-generating function.
 If an element occurs multiple times in the array then the later occurrences are discarded. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.splitInto](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#splitInto)

Array.splitInto 
splitInto 
Splits the input array into at most <code>count</code> chunks. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.empty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#empty)

Array.empty 
empty 
Returns an empty array of the given type. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.exactlyOne](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#exactlyOne)

Array.exactlyOne 
exactlyOne 
Returns the only element of the array. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.tryExactlyOne](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#tryExactlyOne)

Array.tryExactlyOne 
tryExactlyOne 
Returns the only element of the array or <code>None</code> if array is empty or contains more than one element. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.except](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#except)

Array.except 
except 
Returns a new list with the distinct elements of the input array which do not appear in the itemsToExclude sequence,
 using generic hash and equality comparisons to compare values. 
This is an O(n+m) operation using hash-based exclusion.

### [Array.exists](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#exists)

Array.exists 
exists 
Tests if any element of the array satisfies the given predicate. 
The predicate is applied to the elements of the input array. If any application
 returns true then the overall result is true and no further elements are tested.
 Otherwise, false is returned. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.exists2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#exists2)

Array.exists2 
exists2 
Tests if any pair of corresponding elements of the arrays satisfies the given predicate. 
The predicate is applied to matching elements in the two collections up to the lesser of the
 two lengths of the collections. If any application returns true then the overall result is
 true and no further elements are tested. Otherwise, if one collections is longer
 than the other then the <code>ArgumentException</code> exception is raised.
 Otherwise, false is returned. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the arrays.

### [Array.filter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#filter)

Array.filter 
filter 
Returns a new collection containing only the elements of the collection
 for which the given predicate returns "true". 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.find](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#find)

Array.find 
find 
Returns the first element for which the given function returns 'true'.
 Raise <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.keynotfoundexception">KeyNotFoundException</a> if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.findBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#findBack)

Array.findBack 
findBack 
Returns the last element for which the given function returns 'true'.
 Raise <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.keynotfoundexception">KeyNotFoundException</a> if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.findIndex](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#findIndex)

Array.findIndex 
findIndex 
Returns the index of the first element in the array
 that satisfies the given predicate. Raise <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.keynotfoundexception">KeyNotFoundException</a> if
 none of the elements satisfy the predicate. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.findIndexBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#findIndexBack)

Array.findIndexBack 
findIndexBack 
Returns the index of the last element in the array
 that satisfies the given predicate. Raise <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.keynotfoundexception">KeyNotFoundException</a> if
 none of the elements satisfy the predicate. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.forall](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#forall)

Array.forall 
forall 
Tests if all elements of the array satisfy the given predicate. 
The predicate is applied to the elements of the input collection. If any application
 returns false then the overall result is false and no further elements are tested.
 Otherwise, true is returned. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.forall2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#forall2)

Array.forall2 
forall2 
Tests if all corresponding elements of the array satisfy the given predicate pairwise. 
The predicate is applied to matching elements in the two collections up to the lesser of the
 two lengths of the collections. If any application returns false then the overall result is
 false and no further elements are tested. Otherwise, if one collection is longer
 than the other then the <code>ArgumentException</code> exception is raised.
 Otherwise, true is returned. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the arrays.

### [Array.fold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#fold)

Array.fold 
fold 
Applies a function to each element of the collection, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code> then computes
 <code>f (... (f s i0)...) iN</code> 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.foldBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#foldBack)

Array.foldBack 
foldBack 
Applies a function to each element of the array, starting from the end, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code> then computes
 <code>f i0 (...(f iN s))</code> 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.fold2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#fold2)

Array.fold2 
fold2 
Applies a function to pairs of elements drawn from the two collections,
 left-to-right, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. The two input
 arrays must have the same lengths, otherwise an <code>ArgumentException</code> is
 raised. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the arrays.

### [Array.foldBack2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#foldBack2)

Array.foldBack2 
foldBack2 
Apply a function to pairs of elements drawn from the two collections, right-to-left,
 threading an accumulator argument through the computation. The two input
 arrays must have the same lengths, otherwise an <code>ArgumentException</code> is
 raised. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the arrays.

### [Array.get](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#get)

Array.get 
get 
Gets an element from an array. 
Normally the syntax <code>array[index]</code> is preferred. This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.head](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#head)

Array.head 
head 
Returns the first element of the array. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.groupBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#groupBy)

Array.groupBy 
groupBy 
Applies a key-generating function to each element of an array and yields an array of
 unique keys. Each unique key contains an array of all elements that match
 to this key. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.indexed](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#indexed)

Array.indexed 
indexed 
Builds a new array whose elements are the corresponding elements of the input array
 paired with the integer index (from 0) of each element. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.init](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#init)

Array.init 
init 
Creates an array given the dimension and a generator function to compute the elements. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the count.

### [Array.zeroCreate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#zeroCreate)

Array.zeroCreate 
zeroCreate 
Creates an array where the entries are initially the default value Unchecked.defaultof<'T>. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the count.

### [Array.isEmpty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#isEmpty)

Array.isEmpty 
isEmpty 
Returns true if the given array is empty, otherwise false. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.iter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#iter)

Array.iter 
iter 
Applies the given function to each element of the array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.iter2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#iter2)

Array.iter2 
iter2 
Applies the given function to pair of elements drawn from matching indices in two arrays. The
 two arrays must have the same lengths, otherwise an <code>ArgumentException</code> is
 raised. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the arrays.

### [Array.iteri](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#iteri)

Array.iteri 
iteri 
Applies the given function to each element of the array. The integer passed to the
 function indicates the index of element. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.iteri2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#iteri2)

Array.iteri2 
iteri2 
Applies the given function to pair of elements drawn from matching indices in two arrays,
 also passing the index of the elements. The two arrays must have the same lengths,
 otherwise an <code>ArgumentException</code> is raised. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the arrays.

### [Array.last](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#last)

Array.last 
last 
Returns the last element of the array. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.item](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#item)

Array.item 
item 
Gets an element from an array. 
Normally the syntax <code>array[index]</code> is preferred. This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.length](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#length)

Array.length 
length 
Returns the length of an array. You can also use property arr.Length. 
The notation <code>array.Length</code> is preferred. This is an O(1) operation.This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.tryLast](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#tryLast)

Array.tryLast 
tryLast 
Returns the last element of the array.
 Return <code>None</code> if no such element exists. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#map)

Array.map 
map 
Builds a new array whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.map2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#map2)

Array.map2 
map2 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to the corresponding elements of the two collections pairwise. The two input
 arrays must have the same lengths, otherwise an <code>ArgumentException</code> is
 raised. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the arrays.

### [Array.mapFold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#mapFold)

Array.mapFold 
mapFold 
Combines map and fold. Builds a new array whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the input array. The function is also used to accumulate a final value. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.mapFoldBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#mapFoldBack)

Array.mapFoldBack 
mapFoldBack 
Combines map and foldBack. Builds a new array whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the input array. The function is also used to accumulate a final value. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.map3](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#map3)

Array.map3 
map3 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to the corresponding triples from the three collections. The three input
 arrays must have the same length, otherwise an <code>ArgumentException</code> is
 raised. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the arrays.

### [Array.mapi2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#mapi2)

Array.mapi2 
mapi2 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to the corresponding elements of the two collections pairwise, also passing the index of
 the elements. The two input arrays must have the same lengths, otherwise an <code>ArgumentException</code> is
 raised. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the arrays.

### [Array.mapi](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#mapi)

Array.mapi 
mapi 
Builds a new array whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the array. The integer index passed to the
 function indicates the index of element being transformed, starting at zero. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.max](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#max)

Array.max 
max 
Returns the greatest of all elements of the array, compared via Operators.max on the function result. 
Throws ArgumentException for empty arrays. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.maxBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#maxBy)

Array.maxBy 
maxBy 
Returns the greatest of all elements of the array, compared via Operators.max on the function result. 
Returns the first maximal element of the array if there are multiple equal maximum elements.
 Throws ArgumentException for empty arrays. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.min](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#min)

Array.min 
min 
Returns the lowest of all elements of the array, compared via Operators.min. 
Throws ArgumentException for empty arrays. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.minBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#minBy)

Array.minBy 
minBy 
Returns the lowest of all elements of the array, compared via Operators.min on the function result. 
Returns the first minimal element of the array if there are multiple equal minimal elements.
 Throws ArgumentException for empty arrays. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.ofList](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#ofList)

Array.ofList 
ofList 
Builds an array from the given list. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [Array.ofSeq](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#ofSeq)

Array.ofSeq 
ofSeq 
Builds a new array from the given enumerable object. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Array.pairwise](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#pairwise)

Array.pairwise 
pairwise 
Returns an array of each element in the input array paired with its predecessor, with the
 exception of the first element which is only returned as the predecessor of the second element.
 The predecessor comes first in the returned pairs. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.partition](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#partition)

Array.partition 
partition 
Splits the collection into two collections, containing the
 elements for which the given predicate returns "true" and "false"
 respectively. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.partitionWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#partitionWith)

Array.partitionWith 
partitionWith 
Splits the collection into two arrays, by applying the given partitioning function
 to each element. Returns <code>Choice1Of2</code> elements in the first array and
 <code>Choice2Of2</code> elements in the second array. Element order is preserved in both of the created arrays. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.permute](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#permute)

Array.permute 
permute 
Returns an array with all elements permuted according to the
 specified permutation. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.reduce](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#reduce)

Array.reduce 
reduce 
Applies a function to each element of the array, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code>
 then computes <code>f (... (f i0 i1)...) iN</code>.
 Raises ArgumentException if the array has size zero. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.reduceBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#reduceBack)

Array.reduceBack 
reduceBack 
Applies a function to each element of the array, starting from the end, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code>
 then computes <code>f i0 (...(f iN-1 iN))</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.replicate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#replicate)

Array.replicate 
replicate 
Creates an array by replicating the given initial value. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the count.

### [Array.rev](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#rev)

Array.rev 
rev 
Returns a new array with the elements in reverse order. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.scan](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#scan)

Array.scan 
scan 
Like <code>fold</code>, but return the intermediary and final results. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.scanBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#scanBack)

Array.scanBack 
scanBack 
Like <code>foldBack</code>, but return both the intermediary and final results. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.singleton](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#singleton)

Array.singleton 
singleton 
Returns an array that contains one item only. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.set](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#set)

Array.set 
set 
Sets an element of an array. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.skip](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#skip)

Array.skip 
skip 
Builds a new array that contains the elements of the given array, excluding the first N elements. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.skipWhile](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#skipWhile)

Array.skipWhile 
skipWhile 
Bypasses elements in an array while the given predicate returns True, and then returns
 the remaining elements in a new array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.sub](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#sub)

Array.sub 
sub 
Builds a new array that contains the given subrange specified by
 starting index and length. 

 Slicing syntax is generally preferred, e.g.
 <pre class="fssnip highlighted"><code lang="fsharp"> <span class="k">let</span> <span data-fsdocs-tip="fs1" data-fsdocs-tip-unique="1" class="id">input</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="pn">[|</span> <span class="n">0</span><span class="pn">;</span> <span class="n">1</span><span class="pn">;</span> <span class="n">2</span><span class="pn">;</span> <span class="n">3</span><span class="pn">;</span> <span class="n">4</span><span class="pn">;</span> <span class="n">5</span> <span class="pn">|]</span>

 <span data-fsdocs-tip="fs1" data-fsdocs-tip-unique="2" class="id">input</span><span class="pn">.</span><span class="pn">[</span><span class="n">2..</span><span class="n">4</span><span class="pn">]</span>
</code></pre>
<div popover class="fsdocs-tip" id="fs1">val input: int array</div>


  This is an O(count) operation.

### [Array.sort](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#sort)

Array.sort 
sort 
Sorts the elements of an array, returning a new array. Elements are compared using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [Array.sortBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#sortBy)

Array.sortBy 
sortBy 
Sorts the elements of an array, using the given projection for the keys and returning a new array.
 Elements are compared using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [Array.sortWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#sortWith)

Array.sortWith 
sortWith 
Sorts the elements of an array, using the given comparison function as the order, returning a new array.

### [Array.sortInPlaceBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#sortInPlaceBy)

Array.sortInPlaceBy 
sortInPlaceBy 
Sorts the elements of an array by mutating the array in-place, using the given projection for the keys.
 Elements are compared using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [Array.sortInPlaceWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#sortInPlaceWith)

Array.sortInPlaceWith 
sortInPlaceWith 
Sorts the elements of an array by mutating the array in-place, using the given comparison function as the order. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, modifying the array in place.

### [Array.sortInPlace](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#sortInPlace)

Array.sortInPlace 
sortInPlace 
Sorts the elements of an array by mutating the array in-place, using the given comparison function.
 Elements are compared using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, modifying the array in place.

### [Array.splitAt](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#splitAt)

Array.splitAt 
splitAt 
Splits an array into two arrays, at the given index. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.sortDescending](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#sortDescending)

Array.sortDescending 
sortDescending

### [Array.sortByDescending](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#sortByDescending)

Array.sortByDescending 
sortByDescending 
Sorts the elements of an array, in descending order, using the given projection for the keys and returning a new array.
 Elements are compared using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [Array.sum](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#sum)

Array.sum 
sum 
Returns the sum of the elements in the array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.sumBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#sumBy)

Array.sumBy 
sumBy 
Returns the sum of the results generated by applying the function to each element of the array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.take](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#take)

Array.take 
take 
Returns the first N elements of the array. 
Throws <code>InvalidOperationException</code>
 if the count exceeds the number of elements in the array. <code>Array.truncate</code>
 returns as many items as the array contains instead of throwing an exception. This is an O(count) operation.

### [Array.takeWhile](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#takeWhile)

Array.takeWhile 
takeWhile 
Returns an array that contains all elements of the original array while the
 given predicate returns True, and then returns no further elements. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.tail](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#tail)

Array.tail 
tail 
Returns a new array containing the elements of the original except the first element. 
This is an O(n) operation, creating a new array.

### [Array.toList](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#toList)

Array.toList 
toList 
Builds a list from the given array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.toSeq](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#toSeq)

Array.toSeq 
toSeq 
Views the given array as a sequence. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.transpose](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#transpose)

Array.transpose 
transpose 
Returns the transpose of the given sequence of arrays. 
This is an O(n*m) operation, where n and m are the dimensions.

### [Array.truncate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#truncate)

Array.truncate 
truncate 
Returns at most N elements in a new array.

### [Array.tryFind](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#tryFind)

Array.tryFind 
tryFind 
Returns the first element for which the given function returns True.
 Return None if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.tryFindBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#tryFindBack)

Array.tryFindBack 
tryFindBack 
Returns the last element for which the given function returns True.
 Return None if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.tryFindIndex](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#tryFindIndex)

Array.tryFindIndex 
tryFindIndex 
Returns the index of the first element in the array
 that satisfies the given predicate. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.tryItem](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#tryItem)

Array.tryItem 
tryItem 
Tries to find the nth element in the array.
 Returns <code>None</code> if index is negative or the input array does not contain enough elements. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Array.tryFindIndexBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#tryFindIndexBack)

Array.tryFindIndexBack 
tryFindIndexBack 
Returns the index of the last element in the array
 that satisfies the given predicate. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.unfold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#unfold)

Array.unfold 
unfold 
Returns an array that contains the elements generated by the given computation.
 The generator is repeatedly called to build the list until it returns `None`.
 The given initial <code>state</code> argument is passed to the element generator. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of elements generated.

### [Array.unzip](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#unzip)

Array.unzip 
unzip 
Splits an array of pairs into two arrays. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.unzip3](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#unzip3)

Array.unzip3 
unzip3 
Splits an array of triples into three arrays. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.where](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#where)

Array.where 
where 
Returns a new array containing only the elements of the array
 for which the given predicate returns "true". 
This is identical to <code>Array.filter</code>. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.windowed](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#windowed)

windowed 
Returns an array of sliding windows containing elements drawn from the input
 array. Each window is returned as a fresh array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array.zip](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#zip)

Array.zip 
zip 
Combines the two arrays into an array of pairs. The two arrays must have equal lengths, otherwise an <code>ArgumentException</code> is
 raised. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the arrays.

### [Array.zip3](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule.html#zip3)

Array.zip3 
zip3 
Combines three arrays into an array of pairs. The three arrays must have equal lengths, otherwise an <code>ArgumentException</code> is
 raised. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the arrays.

### [Parallel.forall](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#forall)

Parallel.forall 
forall 
Tests if all elements of the array satisfy the given predicate. 
The predicate is applied to the elements of the input collection in parallel. If any application
 returns false then the overall result is false and testing of other elements in all threads is stopped at system's earliest convenience.
 Otherwise, true is returned. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.exists](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#exists)

Parallel.exists 
exists 
Tests if any element of the array satisfies the given predicate. 
The predicate is applied to the elements of the input array in parallel. If any application
 returns true then the overall result is true and testing of other elements in all threads is stopped at system's earliest convenience.
 Otherwise, <code>false</code> is returned. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.tryFind](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#tryFind)

Parallel.tryFind 
tryFind 
Returns the first element for which the given function returns <code>True</code>.
 Returns None if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.tryFindIndex](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#tryFindIndex)

Parallel.tryFindIndex 
tryFindIndex 
Returns the index of the first element in the array
 that satisfies the given predicate.
 Returns <code>None</code> if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.tryPick](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#tryPick)

Parallel.tryPick 
tryPick 
Applies the given function to successive elements, returning the first
 result where the function returns <code>Some(x)</code> for some <code>x</code>. If the function
 never returns <code>Some(x)</code> then <code>None</code> is returned. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.reduce](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#reduce)

Parallel.reduce 
reduce 
Applies a function to each element of the array in parallel, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation for each thread involved in the computation. After processing entire input, results from all threads are reduced together.
 Raises ArgumentException if the array is empty. 
The order of processing is not guaranteed. For that reason, the 'reduce' function argument should be commutative.
 (That is, changing the order of execution must not affect the result)
 Also, compared to the non-parallel version of Array.reduce, the 'reduce' function may be invoked more times due to the resulting reduction from participating threads. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.reduceBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#reduceBy)

Parallel.reduceBy 
reduceBy 
Applies a projection function to each element of the array in parallel, reducing elements in each thread with a dedicated 'reduction' function.
 After processing entire input, results from all threads are reduced together.
 Raises ArgumentException if the array is empty. 
The order of processing is not guaranteed. For that reason, the 'reduction' function argument should be commutative.
 (That is, changing the order of execution must not affect the result) This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.max](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#max)

Parallel.max 
max 
Returns the greatest of all elements of the array, compared via Operators.max. 
Throws ArgumentException for empty arrays. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.maxBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#maxBy)

Parallel.maxBy 
maxBy 
Returns the greatest of all elements of the array, compared via Operators.max on the function result. 
Throws ArgumentException for empty arrays. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.min](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#min)

Parallel.min 
min 
Returns the smallest of all elements of the array, compared via Operators.min. 
Throws ArgumentException for empty arrays This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.minBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#minBy)

Parallel.minBy 
minBy 
Returns the lowest of all elements of the array, compared via Operators.min on the function result. 
Throws ArgumentException for empty arrays. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.sum](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#sum)

Parallel.sum 
sum 
Returns the sum of the elements in the array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.sumBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#sumBy)

Parallel.sumBy 
sumBy 
Returns the sum of the results generated by applying the function to each element of the array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.average](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#average)

Parallel.average 
average 
Returns the average of the elements in the array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.averageBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#averageBy)

Parallel.averageBy 
averageBy 
Returns the average of the elements generated by applying the function to each element of the array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.choose](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#choose)

Parallel.choose 
choose 
Apply the given function to each element of the array. Return
 the array comprised of the results <code>x</code> for each element where
 the function returns <code>Some(x)</code>.

### [Parallel.collect](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#collect)

Parallel.collect 
collect 
For each element of the array, apply the given function. Concatenate all the results and return the combined array. 
Performs the operation in parallel using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html">Parallel.For</a>.
 The order in which the given function is applied to elements of the input array is not specified. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the total output length.

### [Parallel.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#map)

Parallel.map 
map 
Build a new array whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the array.

### [Parallel.mapi](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#mapi)

Parallel.mapi 
mapi 
Build a new array whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the array. The integer index passed to the
 function indicates the index of element being transformed.

### [Parallel.groupBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#groupBy)

Parallel.groupBy 
groupBy 
Applies a key-generating function to each element of an array in parallel and yields an array of
 unique keys. Each unique key contains an array of all elements that match
 to this key. 
Performs the operation in parallel using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html">Parallel.For</a>.
 The order in which the given function is applied to elements of the input array is not specified.
 The order of the keys and values in the result is also not specified. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.iter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#iter)

Parallel.iter 
iter 
Apply the given function to each element of the array.

### [Parallel.iteri](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#iteri)

Parallel.iteri 
iteri 
Apply the given function to each element of the array. The integer passed to the
 function indicates the index of element.

### [Parallel.init](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#init)

Parallel.init 
init 
Create an array given the dimension and a generator function to compute the elements. 
Performs the operation in parallel using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html">Parallel.For</a>.
 The order in which the given function is applied to indices is not specified. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the count.

### [Parallel.partition](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#partition)

Parallel.partition 
partition 
Split the collection into two collections, containing the
 elements for which the given predicate returns "true" and "false"
 respectively  
Performs the operation in parallel using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html">Parallel.For</a>.
 The order in which the given function is applied to indices is not specified. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.partitionWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#partitionWith)

Parallel.partitionWith 
partitionWith 
Splits the collection into two arrays, by applying the given partitioning function
 to each element. Returns <code>Choice1Of2</code> elements in the first array and
 <code>Choice2Of2</code> elements in the second array. Element order is preserved in both of the created arrays. 
Performs the operation in parallel using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html">Parallel.For</a>.
 The order in which the given function is applied to elements of the input array is not specified.
 The partitioner function must be thread-safe. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Parallel.sort](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#sort)

Parallel.sort 
sort 
Sorts the elements of an array in parallel, returning a new array. Elements are compared using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [Parallel.sortBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#sortBy)

Parallel.sortBy 
sortBy 
Sorts the elements of an array in parallel, using the given projection for the keys and returning a new array.
 Elements are compared using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [Parallel.sortWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#sortWith)

Parallel.sortWith 
sortWith 
Sorts the elements of an array in parallel, using the given comparison function as the order, returning a new array.

### [Parallel.sortInPlaceBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#sortInPlaceBy)

Parallel.sortInPlaceBy 
sortInPlaceBy

 Elements are compared using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [Parallel.sortInPlaceWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#sortInPlaceWith)

Parallel.sortInPlaceWith 
sortInPlaceWith 
Sorts the elements of an array by mutating the array in-place in parallel, using the given comparison function as the order. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, modifying the array in place.

### [Parallel.sortInPlace](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#sortInPlace)

Parallel.sortInPlace 
sortInPlace 
Sorts the elements of an array by mutating the array in-place in parallel, using the given comparison function.
 Elements are compared using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, modifying the array in place.

### [Parallel.sortDescending](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#sortDescending)

Parallel.sortDescending 
sortDescending 
Sorts the elements of an array in parallel, in descending order, returning a new array. Elements are compared using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [Parallel.sortByDescending](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#sortByDescending)

Parallel.sortByDescending 
sortByDescending 
Sorts the elements of an array in parallel, in descending order, using the given projection for the keys and returning a new array.
 Elements are compared using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [Parallel.zip](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#zip)

Parallel.zip 
zip 
Combines the two arrays into an array of pairs. The two arrays must have equal lengths, otherwise an <code>ArgumentException</code> is
 raised. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the arrays.

### [Parallel.filter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-arraymodule-parallel.html#filter)

Parallel.filter 
filter 
Returns a new collection containing only the elements of the collection
 for which the given predicate returns <code>true</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Array2D](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-array2dmodule.html)

Array2D 
Contains operations for working with 2-dimensional arrays. 
<p class='fsdocs-para'>See also <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fsharp/language-reference/arrays">F# Language Guide - Arrays</a>.</p><p class='fsdocs-para'>F# and CLI multi-dimensional arrays are typically zero-based.
 However, CLI multi-dimensional arrays used in conjunction with external
 libraries (e.g. libraries associated with Visual Basic) be
 non-zero based, using a potentially different base for each dimension.
 The operations in this module will accept such arrays, and
 the basing on an input array will be propagated to a matching output
 array on the <code>Array2D.map</code> and <code>Array2D.mapi</code> operations.
 Non-zero-based arrays can also be created using <code>Array2D.zeroCreateBased</code>,
 <code>Array2D.createBased</code> and <code>Array2D.initBased</code>.</p> 
Array2D.base1 
base1 
Array2D.base2 
base2

copy 
Array2D.blit 
blit 
Array2D.init 
init 
Array2D.create 
create 
Array2D.zeroCreate 
zeroCreate 
Array2D.initBased 
initBased 
Array2D.createBased 
createBased 
Array2D.zeroCreateBased 
zeroCreateBased 
Array2D.iter 
iter 
Array2D.iteri 
iteri 
Array2D.length1 
length1 
Array2D.length2 
length2

map

mapi

rebase

### [Array2D.base1](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-array2dmodule.html#base1)

Array2D.base1 
base1 
Fetches the base-index for the first dimension of the array.

### [Array2D.base2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-array2dmodule.html#base2)

Array2D.base2 
base2 
Fetches the base-index for the second dimension of the array.

### [Array2D.copy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-array2dmodule.html#copy)

Array2D.copy 
copy 
Builds a new array whose elements are the same as the input array. 
For non-zero-based arrays the basing on an input array will be propagated to the output
 array.

### [Array2D.blit](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-array2dmodule.html#blit)

Array2D.blit 
blit

NonStructural 
Get an implementation of equality semantics using non-structural equality and non-structural hashing.

### [HashIdentity.LimitedStructural](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-hashidentity.html#LimitedStructural)

HashIdentity.LimitedStructural 
LimitedStructural 
Get an implementation of equality semantics using limited structural equality and structural hashing.

### [HashIdentity.Reference](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-hashidentity.html#Reference)

HashIdentity.Reference 
Reference 
Get an implementation of equality semantics using reference equality and reference hashing.

### [HashIdentity.FromFunctions](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-hashidentity.html#FromFunctions)

HashIdentity.FromFunctions 
FromFunctions 
Get an implementation of equality semantics using the given functions.
