### [List.allPairs](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#allPairs)

List.allPairs 
allPairs 
Returns a new list that contains all pairings of elements from two lists. 
This is an O(n*m) operation, where n and m are the lengths of the input lists.

### [List.append](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#append)

List.append 
append 
Returns a new list that contains the elements of the first list
 followed by elements of the second list. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the first list.

### [List.average](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#average)

List.average 
average 
Returns the average of the values in a non-empty list. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.averageBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#averageBy)

List.averageBy 
averageBy 
Returns the average of values in a list generated by applying a function to each element of the list. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.choose](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#choose)

List.choose 
choose 
Applies a function to each element in a list and then returns
 a list of values <code>v</code> where the applied function returned <code>Some(v)</code>.
 
 Returns an empty list when the input list is empty or when the applied chooser function
 returns <code>None</code> for all elements.
  
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.chunkBySize](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#chunkBySize)

List.chunkBySize 
chunkBySize 
Divides the input list into lists (chunks) of size at most <code>chunkSize</code>.
 Returns a new list containing the generated lists (chunks) as its elements.
 
 Returns an empty list when the input list is empty. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.collect](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#collect)

List.collect 
collect 
For each element of the list, applies the given function. Concatenates all the results and returns the combined list. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the total length of all resulting sublists.

### [List.compareWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#compareWith)

List.compareWith 
compareWith 
Compares two lists using the given comparison function, element by element. 
This is an O(min(n,m)) operation, where n and m are the lengths of the lists.

### [List.concat](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#concat)

List.concat 
concat 
Returns a new list that contains the elements of each of the lists in order. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the total number of elements across all lists.

### [List.contains](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#contains)

List.contains 
contains 
Tests if the list contains the specified element. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.distinct](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#distinct)

List.distinct 
distinct 
Returns a list that contains no duplicate entries according to generic hash and
 equality comparisons on the entries.
 If an element occurs multiple times in the list then the later occurrences are discarded. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.distinctBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#distinctBy)

List.distinctBy 
distinctBy 
Returns a list that contains no duplicate entries according to the 
 generic hash and equality comparisons on the keys returned by the given key-generating function.
 If an element occurs multiple times in the list then the later occurrences are discarded. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.countBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#countBy)

List.countBy 
countBy 
Applies a key-generating function to each element of a list and returns a list yielding unique
 keys and their number of occurrences in the original list. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.splitInto](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#splitInto)

List.splitInto 
splitInto 
Splits the input list into at most <code>count</code> chunks. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.empty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#empty)

List.empty 
empty 
Returns an empty list of the given type. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [List.except](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#except)

List.except 
except 
Returns a new list with the distinct elements of the input list which do not appear in the itemsToExclude sequence,
 using generic hash and equality comparisons to compare values. 
This is an O(n+m) operation, where n is the length of the list and m is the length of the items to exclude.

### [List.exactlyOne](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#exactlyOne)

List.exactlyOne 
exactlyOne 
Returns the only element of the list. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [List.tryExactlyOne](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#tryExactlyOne)

List.tryExactlyOne 
tryExactlyOne 
Returns the only element of the list or <code>None</code> if it is empty or contains more than one element. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [List.exists](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#exists)

List.exists 
exists 
Tests if any element of the list satisfies the given predicate. 
The predicate is applied to the elements of the input list. If any application 
 returns true then the overall result is true and no further elements are tested. 
 Otherwise, false is returned. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.exists2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#exists2)

List.exists2 
exists2 
Tests if any pair of corresponding elements of the lists satisfies the given predicate. 
The predicate is applied to matching elements in the two collections up to the lesser of the 
 two lengths of the collections. If any application returns true then the overall result is 
 true and no further elements are tested. Otherwise, if one collections is longer 
 than the other then the <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentexception">ArgumentException</a> exception is raised. 
 Otherwise, false is returned. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the lists.

### [List.find](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#find)

List.find 
find 
Returns the first element for which the given function returns True.
 Raises <code>KeyNotFoundException</code> if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.findBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#findBack)

List.findBack 
findBack 
Returns the last element for which the given function returns True.
 Raises <code>KeyNotFoundException</code> if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.findIndex](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#findIndex)

List.findIndex 
findIndex 
Returns the index of the first element in the list
 that satisfies the given predicate.
 Raises <code>KeyNotFoundException</code> if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.findIndexBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#findIndexBack)

List.findIndexBack 
findIndexBack 
Returns the index of the last element in the list
 that satisfies the given predicate.
 Raises <code>KeyNotFoundException</code> if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.filter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#filter)

List.filter 
filter 
Returns a new collection containing only the elements of the collection
 for which the given predicate returns "true" 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.fold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#fold)

List.fold 
fold 
Applies a function to each element of the collection, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. Take the second argument, and apply the function to it
 and the first element of the list. Then feed this result into the function along
 with the second element and so on. Return the final result.
 If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code> then 
 computes <code>f (... (f s i0) i1 ...) iN</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.fold2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#fold2)

List.fold2 
fold2 
Applies a function to corresponding elements of two collections, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. The collections must have identical sizes.
 If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code> and <code>j0...jN</code>
 then computes <code>f (... (f s i0 j0)...) iN jN</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the lists.

### [List.foldBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#foldBack)

List.foldBack 
foldBack 
Applies a function to each element of the collection, starting from the end, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code> then 
 computes <code>f i0 (...(f iN s))</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.foldBack2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#foldBack2)

List.foldBack2 
foldBack2 
Applies a function to corresponding elements of two collections, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. The collections must have identical sizes.
 If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code> and <code>j0...jN</code>
 then computes <code>f i0 j0 (...(f iN jN s))</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the lists.

### [List.forall](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#forall)

List.forall 
forall 
Tests if all elements of the collection satisfy the given predicate. 
The predicate is applied to the elements of the input list. If any application 
 returns false then the overall result is false and no further elements are tested. 
 Otherwise, true is returned. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.forall2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#forall2)

List.forall2 
forall2 
Tests if all corresponding elements of the collection satisfy the given predicate pairwise. 
The predicate is applied to matching elements in the two collections up to the lesser of the 
 two lengths of the collections. If any application returns false then the overall result is 
 false and no further elements are tested. Otherwise, if one collection is longer 
 than the other then the <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentexception">ArgumentException</a> exception is raised. 
 Otherwise, true is returned. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the lists.

### [List.groupBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#groupBy)

List.groupBy 
groupBy 
Applies a key-generating function to each element of a list and yields a list of 
 unique keys. Each unique key contains a list of all elements that match 
 to this key. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.head](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#head)

List.head 
head 
Returns the first element of the list. 
Lists are represented as linked lists so this is an O(1) operation.

### [List.indexed](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#indexed)

List.indexed 
indexed 
Returns a new list whose elements are the corresponding elements
 of the input list paired with the index (from 0) of each element. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.init](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#init)

List.init 
init 
Creates a list by calling the given generator on each index. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the specified count.

### [List.isEmpty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#isEmpty)

List.isEmpty 
isEmpty 
Returns true if the list contains no elements, false otherwise. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [List.item](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#item)

List.item 
item 
Indexes into the list. The first element has index 0. 
Lists are represented as linked lists so this is an O(n) operation, where n is the index.

### [List.iter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#iter)

List.iter 
iter 
Applies the given function to each element of the collection. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.iter2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#iter2)

List.iter2 
iter2 
Applies the given function to two collections simultaneously. The
 collections must have identical sizes. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the lists.

### [List.iteri](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#iteri)

List.iteri 
iteri 
Applies the given function to each element of the collection. The integer passed to the
 function indicates the index of the element. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.iteri2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#iteri2)

List.iteri2 
iteri2 
Applies the given function to two collections simultaneously. The
 collections must have identical sizes. The integer passed to the
 function indicates the index of the element. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the lists.

### [List.last](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#last)

List.last 
last 
Returns the last element of the list. 
Lists are represented as linked lists so this is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.length](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#length)

List.length 
length 
Returns the length of the list. 
The notation <code>list.Length</code> is preferred. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.tryLast](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#tryLast)

List.tryLast 
tryLast 
Returns the last element of the list.
 Return <code>None</code> if no such element exists. 
Lists are represented as linked lists so this is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#map)

List.map 
map 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the collection. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.map2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#map2)

List.map2 
map2 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to the corresponding elements of the two collections pairwise. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the lists.

### [List.map3](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#map3)

List.map3 
map3 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to the corresponding elements of the three collections simultaneously. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the lists.

### [List.mapFold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#mapFold)

List.mapFold 
mapFold 
Combines map and fold. Builds a new list whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the input list. The function is also used to accumulate a final value. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.mapFoldBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#mapFoldBack)

List.mapFoldBack 
mapFoldBack 
Combines map and foldBack. Builds a new list whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the input list. The function is also used to accumulate a final value. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.mapi](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#mapi)

List.mapi 
mapi 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the collection. The integer index passed to the
 function indicates the index (from 0) of the element being transformed. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.mapi2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#mapi2)

List.mapi2 
mapi2 
Like mapi, but mapping corresponding elements from two lists of equal length. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the lists.

### [List.max](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#max)

List.max 
max 
Return the greatest of all elements of the list, compared via Operators.max. 
Raises <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentexception">ArgumentException</a> if <code>list</code> is empty. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.maxBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#maxBy)

List.maxBy 
maxBy 
Returns the greatest of all elements of the list, compared via Operators.max on the function result. 
Returns the first maximal element of the list if there are multiple equal maximum elements.
 Raises <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentexception">ArgumentException</a> if <code>list</code> is empty. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.min](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#min)

List.min 
min 
Returns the lowest of all elements of the list, compared via Operators.min. 
Raises <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentexception">ArgumentException</a> if <code>list</code> is empty This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.minBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#minBy)

List.minBy 
minBy 
Returns the lowest of all elements of the list, compared via Operators.min on the function result 
Returns the first minimal element of the list if there are multiple equal minimal elements.
 Raises <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentexception">ArgumentException</a> if <code>list</code> is empty. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.nth](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#nth)

List.nth 
nth 
Indexes into the list. The first element has index 0. 
Lists are represented as linked lists so this is an O(n) operation, where n is the index.

### [List.ofArray](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#ofArray)

List.ofArray 
ofArray 
Builds a list from the given array. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [List.ofSeq](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#ofSeq)

List.ofSeq 
ofSeq 
Builds a new list from the given enumerable object. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [List.pairwise](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#pairwise)

List.pairwise 
pairwise 
Returns a list of each element in the input list paired with its predecessor, with the
 exception of the first element which is only returned as the predecessor of the second element.
 The predecessor comes first in the returned pairs. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.partition](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#partition)

List.partition 
partition 
Splits the collection into two collections, containing the 
 elements for which the given predicate returns True and False
 respectively. Element order is preserved in both of the created lists. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.partitionWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#partitionWith)

List.partitionWith 
partitionWith 
Splits the collection into two collections, by applying the given partitioning function
 to each element. Returns <code>Choice1Of2</code> elements in the first list and
 <code>Choice2Of2</code> elements in the second list. Element order is preserved in both of the created lists. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.pick](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#pick)

List.pick 
pick 
Applies the given function to successive elements, returning the first
 result where function returns <code>Some(x)</code> for some x. If no such
 element exists then raise <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.keynotfoundexception">KeyNotFoundException</a> 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.permute](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#permute)

List.permute 
permute 
Returns a list with all elements permuted according to the
 specified permutation. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.reduce](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#reduce)

List.reduce 
reduce 
Apply a function to each element of the collection, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. Apply the function to the first two elements of the list.
 Then feed this result into the function along with the third element and so on. 
 Return the final result. If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code> then computes 
 <code>f (... (f i0 i1) i2 ...) iN</code>. 
Raises <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.argumentexception">ArgumentException</a> if <code>list</code> is empty. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.reduceBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#reduceBack)

List.reduceBack 
reduceBack 
Applies a function to each element of the collection, starting from the end, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code> then computes 
 <code>f i0 (...(f iN-1 iN))</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.replicate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#replicate)

List.replicate 
replicate 
Creates a list by replicating the given initial value. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the specified count.

### [List.rev](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#rev)

List.rev 
rev 
Returns a new list with the elements in reverse order. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.scan](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#scan)

List.scan 
scan 
Applies a function to each element of the collection, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. Take the second argument, and apply the function to it
 and the first element of the list. Then feed this result into the function along
 with the second element and so on. Returns the list of intermediate results and the final result. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.scanBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#scanBack)

List.scanBack 
scanBack 
Like <code>foldBack</code>, but returns both the intermediary and final results 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.singleton](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#singleton)

List.singleton 
singleton 
Returns a list that contains one item only. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [List.skip](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#skip)

List.skip 
skip 
Returns the list after removing the first N elements. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of elements to skip.

### [List.skipWhile](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#skipWhile)

List.skipWhile 
skipWhile 
Bypasses elements in a list while the given predicate returns True, and then returns
 the remaining elements of the list. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.sortWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#sortWith)

sortWith 
Sorts the given list using the given comparison function.

sortByDescending 
Sorts the given list in descending order using keys given by the given projection. Keys are compared using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [List.sortDescending](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#sortDescending)

List.sortDescending

Sorts the given list in descending order using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [List.tail](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#tail)

Lists are represented as linked lists so this is an O(1) operation.

### [List.take](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#take)

List.take 
take 
Returns the first N elements of the list. 
Throws <code>InvalidOperationException</code>
 if the count exceeds the number of elements in the list. <code>List.truncate</code>
 returns as many items as the list contains instead of throwing an exception. This is an O(count) operation.

### [List.takeWhile](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#takeWhile)

takeWhile 
Returns a list that contains all elements of the original list while the 
 given predicate returns True, and then returns no further elements. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the list.

 exists then return <code>None</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the list.

### [List.tryFind](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#tryFind)

### [List.unfold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html#unfold)

List.unfold 
unfold 
Returns a list that contains the elements generated by the given computation.
 The generator is repeatedly called to build the list until it returns <code>None</code>.
 The given initial <code>state</code> argument is passed to the element generator.  
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of elements generated.

 for which the given predicate returns "true"

### [Map.add](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#add)

Map.add 
add 
Returns a new map with the binding added to the given map.
 If a binding with the given key already exists in the input map, the existing binding is replaced by the new binding in the result map. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.change](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#change)

Map.change 
change 
Returns a new map with the value stored under key changed according to f. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.ofList](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#ofList)

Map.ofList 
ofList 
Returns a new map made from the given bindings. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, where n is the length of the list.

### [Map.ofArray](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#ofArray)

Map.ofArray 
ofArray 
Returns a new map made from the given bindings. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, where n is the length of the array.

### [Map.ofSeq](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#ofSeq)

Map.ofSeq 
ofSeq 
Returns a new map made from the given bindings. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the sequence.

### [Map.toSeq](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#toSeq)

Map.toSeq 
toSeq 
Views the collection as an enumerable sequence of pairs.
 The sequence will be ordered by the keys of the map. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.toList](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#toList)

Map.toList 
toList 
Returns a list of all key-value pairs in the mapping.
 The list will be ordered by the keys of the map. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.toArray](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#toArray)

Map.toArray 
toArray 
Returns an array of all key-value pairs in the mapping.
 The array will be ordered by the keys of the map. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.isEmpty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#isEmpty)

Map.isEmpty 
isEmpty 
Is the map empty? 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Map.empty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#empty)

Map.empty 
empty 
The empty map. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Map.find](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#find)

Map.find 
find 
Lookup an element in the map, raising <code>KeyNotFoundException</code> if no binding
 exists in the map. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.tryPick](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#tryPick)

Map.tryPick 
tryPick 
Searches the map looking for the first element where the given function returns a <code>Some</code> value. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.pick](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#pick)

Map.pick 
pick 
Searches the map looking for the first element where the given function returns a <code>Some</code> value.
 Raise <code>KeyNotFoundException</code> if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.foldBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#foldBack)

Map.foldBack 
foldBack 
Folds over the bindings in the map. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.fold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#fold)

Map.fold 
fold 
Folds over the bindings in the map  
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.iter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#iter)

Map.iter 
iter 
Applies the given function to each binding in the dictionary 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.exists](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#exists)

Map.exists 
exists 
Returns true if the given predicate returns true for one of the
 bindings in the map. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.filter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#filter)

Map.filter 
filter 
Builds a new map containing only the bindings for which the given predicate returns 'true'. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.forall](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#forall)

Map.forall 
forall 
Returns true if the given predicate returns true for all of the
 bindings in the map. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#map)

Map.map 
map 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the collection. The key passed to the
 function indicates the key of element being transformed. 
This is an O(n) operation, creating a new map with the same keys.

### [Map.containsKey](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#containsKey)

Map.containsKey 
containsKey 
Tests if an element is in the domain of the map. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.partition](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#partition)

Map.partition 
partition 
Builds two new maps, one containing the bindings for which the given predicate returns 'true',
 and the other the remaining bindings. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.remove](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#remove)

Map.remove 
remove 
Removes an element from the domain of the map. No exception is raised if the element is not present. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.tryFind](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#tryFind)

Map.tryFind 
tryFind 
Lookup an element in the map, returning a <code>Some</code> value if the element is in the domain
 of the map and <code>None</code> if not. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.findKey](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#findKey)

Map.findKey 
findKey 
Evaluates the function on each mapping in the collection. Returns the key for the first mapping
 where the function returns 'true'. Raise <code>KeyNotFoundException</code> if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.tryFindKey](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#tryFindKey)

Map.tryFindKey 
tryFindKey 
Returns the key of the first mapping in the collection that satisfies the given predicate.
 Returns 'None' if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.count](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#count)

Map.count 
count 
The number of bindings in the map. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.keys](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#keys)

Map.keys 
keys 
The keys in the map.
 The sequence will be ordered by the keys of the map. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.values](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#values)

Map.values 
values 
The values in the map, including the duplicates.
 The sequence will be ordered by the keys of the map. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.minKeyValue](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#minKeyValue)

Map.minKeyValue 
minKeyValue 
Returns binding for the smallest key in the map.
 Raise <code>KeyNotFoundException</code> when map is empty. 
This is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map.maxKeyValue](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html#maxKeyValue)

Map.maxKeyValue 
maxKeyValue 
Returns binding for the largest key in the map.
 Raise <code>KeyNotFoundException</code> when map is empty. 
This is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.
