### [Seq.allPairs](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#allPairs)

Seq.allPairs 
allPairs 
Returns a new sequence that contains all pairings of elements from the first and second sequences. 
Enumeration is O(n*m), where n and m are the lengths of the sequences.

### [Seq.append](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#append)

Seq.append 
append 
Wraps the two given enumerations as a single concatenated
 enumeration. 
The returned sequence may be passed between threads safely. However,
 individual IEnumerator values generated from the returned sequence should not be accessed
 concurrently. Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n+m), where n and m are the lengths of the sequences.

### [Seq.average](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#average)

Seq.average 
average 
Returns the average of the elements in the sequence. 
The elements are averaged using the <code>+</code> operator, <code>DivideByInt</code> method and <code>Zero</code> property
 associated with the element type. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.averageBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#averageBy)

Seq.averageBy 
averageBy 
Returns the average of the results generated by applying the function to each element
 of the sequence. 
The elements are averaged using the <code>+</code> operator, <code>DivideByInt</code> method and <code>Zero</code> property
 associated with the generated type. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.cache](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#cache)

Seq.cache 
cache 
Returns a sequence that corresponds to a cached version of the input sequence. 

 The result sequence will have the same elements as the input sequence. The result
 can be enumerated multiple times. The input sequence will be enumerated at most
 once and only as far as is necessary.  Caching a sequence is typically useful when repeatedly
 evaluating items in the original sequence is computationally expensive or if
 iterating the sequence causes side-effects that the user does not want to be
 repeated multiple times.

 Enumeration of the result sequence is thread safe in the sense that multiple independent IEnumerator
 values may be used simultaneously from different threads (accesses to
 the internal lookaside table are thread safe). Each individual IEnumerator
 is not typically thread safe and should not be accessed concurrently.

 Once enumeration of the input sequence has started,
 it's enumerator will be kept live by this object until the enumeration has completed.
 At that point, the enumerator will be disposed.

 The enumerator may be disposed and underlying cache storage released by
 converting the returned sequence object to type IDisposable, and calling the Dispose method
 on this object. The sequence object may then be re-enumerated and a fresh enumerator will
 be used.

 Caching requires O(k) space for k accessed elements.

### [Seq.cast](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#cast)

Seq.cast 
cast 
Wraps a loosely-typed System.Collections sequence as a typed sequence. 
The use of this function usually requires a type annotation.
 An incorrect type annotation may result in runtime type
 errors.
 Individual IEnumerator values generated from the returned sequence should not be accessed concurrently. Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.choose](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#choose)

Seq.choose 
choose 
Applies the given function to each element of the sequence. Returns
 a sequence comprised of the results "x" for each element where
 the function returns Some(x). 
The returned sequence may be passed between threads safely. However,
 individual IEnumerator values generated from the returned sequence should not
 be accessed concurrently. Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.chunkBySize](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#chunkBySize)

Seq.chunkBySize 
chunkBySize 
Divides the input sequence into chunks of size at most <code>chunkSize</code>. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.collect](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#collect)

Seq.collect 
collect 
Applies the given function to each element of the sequence and concatenates all the
 results. 
Remember sequence is lazy, effects are delayed until it is enumerated. Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.compareWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#compareWith)

Seq.compareWith 
compareWith 
Compares two sequences using the given comparison function, element by element. 
This is an O(min(n,m)) operation, where n and m are the lengths of the sequences.

### [Seq.concat](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#concat)

Seq.concat 
concat 
Combines the given enumeration-of-enumerations as a single concatenated
 enumeration. 
The returned sequence may be passed between threads safely. However,
 individual IEnumerator values generated from the returned sequence should not be accessed concurrently. Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the total number of elements.

### [Seq.contains](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#contains)

Seq.contains 
contains 
Tests if the sequence contains the specified element. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.countBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#countBy)

Seq.countBy 
countBy 
Applies a key-generating function to each element of a sequence and returns a sequence yielding unique
 keys and their number of occurrences in the original sequence. 
Note that this function returns a sequence that digests the whole initial sequence as soon as
 that sequence is iterated. As a result this function should not be used with
 large or infinite sequences. The function makes no assumption on the ordering of the original
 sequence. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.delay](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#delay)

Seq.delay 
delay 
Returns a sequence that is built from the given delayed specification of a
 sequence. 
The input function is evaluated each time an IEnumerator for the sequence
 is requested. Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration cost depends on the generated sequence.

### [Seq.distinct](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#distinct)

Seq.distinct 
distinct 
Returns a sequence that contains no duplicate entries according to generic hash and
 equality comparisons on the entries.
 If an element occurs multiple times in the sequence then the later occurrences are discarded. 
This operation requires O(k) space where k is the number of distinct elements seen.

### [Seq.distinctBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#distinctBy)

Seq.distinctBy 
distinctBy 
Returns a sequence that contains no duplicate entries according to the
 generic hash and equality comparisons on the keys returned by the given key-generating function.
 If an element occurs multiple times in the sequence then the later occurrences are discarded. 
This operation requires O(k) space where k is the number of distinct keys seen.

### [Seq.splitInto](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#splitInto)

Seq.splitInto 
splitInto 
Splits the input sequence into at most <code>count</code> chunks. 
This function returns a sequence that digests the whole initial sequence as soon as that
 sequence is iterated. As a result this function should not be used with large or infinite sequences. This function consumes the whole input sequence before yielding the first element of the result sequence. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.empty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#empty)

Seq.empty 
empty 
Creates an empty sequence. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Seq.except](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#except)

Seq.except 
except 
Returns a new sequence with the distinct elements of the second sequence which do not appear in the first sequence,
 using generic hash and equality comparisons to compare values. 
Note that this function returns a sequence that digests the whole of the first input sequence as soon as
 the result sequence is iterated. As a result this function should not be used with
 large or infinite sequences in the first parameter. The function makes no assumption on the ordering of the first input
 sequence. This is an O(n+m) operation using hash-based exclusion.

### [Seq.exists](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#exists)

Seq.exists 
exists 
Tests if any element of the sequence satisfies the given predicate. 
The predicate is applied to the elements of the input sequence. If any application
 returns true then the overall result is true and no further elements are tested.
 Otherwise, false is returned. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.exists2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#exists2)

Seq.exists2 
exists2 
Tests if any pair of corresponding elements of the input sequences satisfies the given predicate. 
The predicate is applied to matching elements in the two sequences up to the lesser of the
 two lengths of the collections. If any application returns true then the overall result is
 true and no further elements are tested. Otherwise, false is returned. If one sequence is shorter than
 the other then the remaining elements of the longer sequence are ignored. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequences.

### [Seq.filter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#filter)

Seq.filter 
filter 
Returns a new collection containing only the elements of the collection
 for which the given predicate returns "true". This is a synonym for Seq.where. 
The returned sequence may be passed between threads safely. However,
 individual IEnumerator values generated from the returned sequence should not be accessed concurrently.

 Remember sequence is lazy, effects are delayed until it is enumerated. Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.where](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#where)

Seq.where 
where 
Returns a new collection containing only the elements of the collection
 for which the given predicate returns "true". 
The returned sequence may be passed between threads safely. However,
 individual IEnumerator values generated from the returned sequence should not be accessed concurrently.

 Remember sequence is lazy, effects are delayed until it is enumerated.

 A synonym for Seq.filter. Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.find](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#find)

Seq.find 
find 
Returns the first element for which the given function returns True. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.findBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#findBack)

Seq.findBack 
findBack 
Returns the last element for which the given function returns True. 
This function digests the whole initial sequence as soon as it is called. As a
 result this function should not be used with large or infinite sequences. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.findIndex](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#findIndex)

Seq.findIndex 
findIndex 
Returns the index of the first element for which the given function returns True. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.findIndexBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#findIndexBack)

Seq.findIndexBack 
findIndexBack 
Returns the index of the last element for which the given function returns True. 
This function digests the whole initial sequence as soon as it is called. As a
 result this function should not be used with large or infinite sequences. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.fold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#fold)

Seq.fold 
fold 
Applies a function to each element of the collection, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code>
 then computes <code>f (... (f s i0)...) iN</code> 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.fold2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#fold2)

Seq.fold2 
fold2 
Applies a function to corresponding elements of two collections, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. 
 The two sequences need not have equal lengths:
 when one sequence is exhausted any remaining elements in the other sequence are ignored.
 If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code> and <code>j0...jN</code>
 then computes <code>f (... (f s i0 j0)...) iN jN</code>. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequences.

### [Seq.foldBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#foldBack)

Seq.foldBack 
foldBack 
Applies a function to each element of the collection, starting from the end, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code>
 then computes <code>f i0 (... (f iN s)...)</code> 
This function consumes the whole input sequence before returning the result. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.foldBack2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#foldBack2)

Seq.foldBack2 
foldBack2 
Applies a function to corresponding elements of two collections, starting from the end of the shorter collection,
 threading an accumulator argument through the computation. The two sequences need not have equal lengths.
 If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code> and <code>j0...jM</code>, N < M
 then computes <code>f i0 j0 (... (f iN jN s)...)</code>. 

 This function consumes the whole of both inputs sequences before returning the result. As a
 result this function should not be used with large or infinite sequences. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequences.

### [Seq.forall](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#forall)

Seq.forall 
forall 
Tests if all elements of the sequence satisfy the given predicate. 
The predicate is applied to the elements of the input sequence. If any application
 returns false then the overall result is false and no further elements are tested.
 Otherwise, true is returned. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.forall2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#forall2)

Seq.forall2 
forall2 
Tests the all pairs of elements drawn from the two sequences satisfy the
 given predicate. If one sequence is shorter than
 the other then the remaining elements of the longer sequence are ignored. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequences.

### [Seq.groupBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#groupBy)

Seq.groupBy 
groupBy 
Applies a key-generating function to each element of a sequence and yields a sequence of
 unique keys. Each unique key contains a sequence of all elements that match
 to this key. 
This function returns a sequence that digests the whole initial sequence as soon as
 that sequence is iterated. As a result this function should not be used with
 large or infinite sequences. The function makes no assumption on the ordering of the original
 sequence. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.head](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#head)

Seq.head 
head 
Returns the first element of the sequence. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Seq.tryHead](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#tryHead)

Seq.tryHead 
tryHead 
Returns the first element of the sequence, or None if the sequence is empty. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Seq.last](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#last)

Seq.last 
last 
Returns the last element of the sequence. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.tryLast](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#tryLast)

Seq.tryLast 
tryLast 
Returns the last element of the sequence.
 Return <code>None</code> if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.exactlyOne](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#exactlyOne)

Seq.exactlyOne 
exactlyOne 
Returns the only element of the sequence. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Seq.tryExactlyOne](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#tryExactlyOne)

Seq.tryExactlyOne 
tryExactlyOne 
Returns the only element of the sequence or <code>None</code> if sequence is empty or contains more than one element. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Seq.isEmpty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#isEmpty)

Seq.isEmpty 
isEmpty 
Returns true if the sequence contains no elements, false otherwise. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Seq.indexed](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#indexed)

Seq.indexed 
indexed 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the corresponding elements of the input collection
 paired with the integer index (from 0) of each element. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.init](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#init)

Seq.init 
init 
Generates a new sequence which, when iterated, will return successive
 elements by calling the given function, up to the given count. The results of calling the function
 will not be saved, that is the function will be reapplied as necessary to
 regenerate the elements. The function is passed the index of the item being
 generated. To cache the results, see <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html">Seq.Cache</a>. 
The returned sequence may be passed between threads safely. However,
 individual IEnumerator values generated from the returned sequence should not be accessed concurrently.
 Construction of the sequence object is an O(1) operation. Each enumeration is an O(n) operation, where n is the count,
 invoking the initializer function once per element.

### [Seq.initInfinite](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#initInfinite)

Seq.initInfinite 
initInfinite 
Generates a new sequence which, when iterated, will return successive
 elements by calling the given function.  The results of calling the function
 will not be saved, that is the function will be reapplied as necessary to
 regenerate the elements.  The function is passed the index of the item being
 generated. 
The returned sequence may be passed between threads safely. However,
 individual IEnumerator values generated from the returned sequence should not be accessed concurrently.
 Iteration can continue up to <code>Int32.MaxValue</code>. This is an O(1) operation.

### [Seq.item](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#item)

Seq.item 
item 
Computes the element at the specified index in the collection. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the index.

### [Seq.iter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#iter)

Seq.iter 
iter 
Applies the given function to each element of the collection. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.iteri](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#iteri)

Seq.iteri 
iteri 
Applies the given function to each element of the collection. The integer passed to the
 function indicates the index of element. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.iter2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#iter2)

Seq.iter2 
iter2 
Applies the given function to two collections simultaneously. If one sequence is shorter than
 the other then the remaining elements of the longer sequence are ignored. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequences.

### [Seq.iteri2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#iteri2)

Seq.iteri2 
iteri2 
Applies the given function to two collections simultaneously. If one sequence is shorter than
 the other then the remaining elements of the longer sequence are ignored. The integer passed to the
 function indicates the index of element. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequences.

### [Seq.length](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#length)

Seq.length 
length 
Returns the length of the sequence 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#map)

Seq.map 
map 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the collection.  The given function will be applied
 as elements are demanded using the <code>MoveNext</code> method on enumerators retrieved from the
 object. 
The returned sequence may be passed between threads safely. However,
 individual IEnumerator values generated from the returned sequence should not be accessed concurrently. Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.map2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#map2)

Seq.map2 
map2 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to the corresponding pairs of elements from the two sequences. If one input sequence is shorter than
 the other then the remaining elements of the longer sequence are ignored. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequences.

### [Seq.mapFold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#mapFold)

Seq.mapFold 
mapFold 
Combines map and fold. Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the collection. The function is also used to accumulate a final value. 
This function digests the whole initial sequence as soon as it is called. As a result this function should
 not be used with large or infinite sequences. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.mapFoldBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#mapFoldBack)

Seq.mapFoldBack 
mapFoldBack 
Combines map and foldBack. Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the collection. The function is also used to accumulate a final value. 
This function digests the whole initial sequence as soon as it is called. As a result this function should
 not be used with large or infinite sequences. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.map3](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#map3)

Seq.map3 
map3 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to the corresponding triples of elements from the three sequences. If one input sequence if shorter than
 the others then the remaining elements of the longer sequences are ignored. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequences.

### [Seq.mapi](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#mapi)

Seq.mapi 
mapi 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to each of the elements of the collection. The integer index passed to the
 function indicates the index (from 0) of element being transformed. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.mapi2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#mapi2)

Seq.mapi2 
mapi2 
Builds a new collection whose elements are the results of applying the given function
 to the corresponding pairs of elements from the two sequences. If one input sequence is shorter than
 the other then the remaining elements of the longer sequence are ignored. The integer index passed to the
 function indicates the index (from 0) of element being transformed. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequences.

### [Seq.max](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#max)

Seq.max 
max 
Returns the greatest of all elements of the sequence, compared via Operators.max 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.maxBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#maxBy)

Seq.maxBy 
maxBy 
Returns the greatest of all elements of the sequence, compared via Operators.max on the function result. 
Returns the first maximal element of the sequence if there are multiple equal maximum elements.
 This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.min](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#min)

Seq.min 
min 
Returns the lowest of all elements of the sequence, compared via <code>Operators.min</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.minBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#minBy)

Seq.minBy 
minBy 
Returns the lowest of all elements of the sequence, compared via Operators.min on the function result. 
Returns the first minimal element of the sequence if there are multiple equal minimal elements.
 This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.nth](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#nth)

Seq.nth 
nth 
Computes the nth element in the collection. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the index.

### [Seq.ofArray](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#ofArray)

Seq.ofArray 
ofArray 
Views the given array as a sequence. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the array.

### [Seq.ofList](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#ofList)

Seq.ofList 
ofList 
Views the given list as a sequence. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Seq.pairwise](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#pairwise)

Seq.pairwise 
pairwise 
Returns a sequence of each element in the input sequence paired with its predecessor, with the
 exception of the first element which is only returned as the predecessor of the second element.
 The predecessor comes first in the returned pairs. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.permute](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#permute)

Seq.permute 
permute 
Returns a sequence with all elements permuted according to the
 specified permutation. 
This function consumes the whole input sequence before yielding the first element of the result sequence. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.pick](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#pick)

Seq.pick 
pick 
Applies the given function to successive elements, returning the first
 <code>x</code> where the function returns "Some(x)". 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.readonly](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#readonly)

Seq.readonly 
readonly 
Builds a new sequence object that delegates to the given sequence object. This ensures
 the original sequence cannot be rediscovered and mutated by a type cast. For example,
 if given an array the returned sequence will return the elements of the array, but
 you cannot cast the returned sequence object to an array. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.reduce](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#reduce)

Seq.reduce 
reduce 
Applies a function to each element of the sequence, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. Begin by applying the function to the first two elements.
 Then feed this result into the function along with the third element and so on.
 Return the final result. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.replicate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#replicate)

Seq.replicate 
replicate 
Creates a sequence by replicating the given initial value. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(count).

### [Seq.reduceBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#reduceBack)

Seq.reduceBack 
reduceBack 
Applies a function to each element of the sequence, starting from the end, threading an accumulator argument
 through the computation. If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code>
 then computes <code>f i0 (...(f iN-1 iN))</code>. 
This function consumes the whole input sequence before returning the result. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.rev](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#rev)

Seq.rev 
rev 
Returns a new sequence with the elements in reverse order. 
This function consumes the whole input sequence before yielding the first element of the reversed sequence. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.scan](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#scan)

Seq.scan 
scan 
Like fold, but computes on-demand and returns the sequence of intermediary and final results. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.scanBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#scanBack)

Seq.scanBack 
scanBack 
Like <code>foldBack</code>, but returns the sequence of intermediary and final results. 
This function returns a sequence that digests the whole initial sequence as soon as that
 sequence is iterated. As a result this function should not be used with large or infinite sequences.
 This function consumes the whole input sequence before returning the result. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.singleton](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#singleton)

Seq.singleton 
singleton 
Returns a sequence yielding one item only. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Seq.skip](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#skip)

Seq.skip 
skip 
Returns a sequence that skips N elements of the underlying sequence and then yields the
 remaining elements of the sequence. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the count.

### [Seq.skipWhile](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#skipWhile)

Seq.skipWhile 
skipWhile 
Returns a sequence that, when iterated, skips elements of the underlying sequence while the
 given predicate returns True, and then yields the remaining elements of the sequence. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.sort](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#sort)

Seq.sort 
sort 
Yields a sequence ordered by keys.

### [Seq.sortWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#sortWith)

Seq.sortWith 
sortWith 
Yields a sequence ordered using the given comparison function.

### [Seq.sortBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#sortBy)

Seq.sortBy 
sortBy 
Applies a key-generating function to each element of a sequence and yield a sequence ordered
 by keys.  The keys are compared using generic comparison as implemented by <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [Seq.sortDescending](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#sortDescending)

Seq.sortDescending 
sortDescending 
Yields a sequence ordered descending by keys.

### [Seq.sortByDescending](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#sortByDescending)

Seq.sortByDescending 
sortByDescending 
Applies a key-generating function to each element of a sequence and yield a sequence ordered
 descending by keys.  The keys are compared using generic comparison as implemented by <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#compare">Operators.compare</a>.

### [Seq.sum](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#sum)

Seq.sum 
sum 
Returns the sum of the elements in the sequence. 
The elements are summed using the <code>+</code> operator and <code>Zero</code> property associated with the generated type. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.sumBy](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#sumBy)

Seq.sumBy 
sumBy 
Returns the sum of the results generated by applying the function to each element of the sequence. 
The generated elements are summed using the <code>+</code> operator and <code>Zero</code> property associated with the generated type. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.tail](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#tail)

Seq.tail 
tail 
Returns a sequence that skips 1 element of the underlying sequence and then yields the
 remaining elements of the sequence. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.take](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#take)

Seq.take 
take 
Returns the first N elements of the sequence. 
Throws <code>InvalidOperationException</code>
 if the count exceeds the number of elements in the sequence. <code>Seq.truncate</code>
 returns as many items as the sequence contains instead of throwing an exception. Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(count).

### [Seq.takeWhile](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#takeWhile)

Seq.takeWhile 
takeWhile 
Returns a sequence that, when iterated, yields elements of the underlying sequence while the
 given predicate returns True, and then returns no further elements. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.toArray](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#toArray)

Seq.toArray 
toArray 
Builds an array from the given collection. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.toList](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#toList)

Seq.toList 
toList 
Builds a list from the given collection. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.tryFind](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#tryFind)

Seq.tryFind 
tryFind 
Returns the first element for which the given function returns True.
 Return None if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.tryFindBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#tryFindBack)

Seq.tryFindBack 
tryFindBack 
Returns the last element for which the given function returns True.
 Return None if no such element exists. 
This function digests the whole initial sequence as soon as it is called. As a
 result this function should not be used with large or infinite sequences. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.tryFindIndex](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#tryFindIndex)

Seq.tryFindIndex 
tryFindIndex 
Returns the index of the first element in the sequence
 that satisfies the given predicate. Return <code>None</code> if no such element exists. 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.tryItem](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#tryItem)

Seq.tryItem 
tryItem 
Tries to find the nth element in the sequence.
 Returns <code>None</code> if index is negative or the input sequence does not contain enough elements. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the index.

### [Seq.tryFindIndexBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#tryFindIndexBack)

Seq.tryFindIndexBack 
tryFindIndexBack 
Returns the index of the last element in the sequence
 that satisfies the given predicate. Return <code>None</code> if no such element exists. 
This function digests the whole initial sequence as soon as it is called. As a
 result this function should not be used with large or infinite sequences. This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.tryPick](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#tryPick)

Seq.tryPick 
tryPick 
Applies the given function to successive elements, returning the first
 result where the function returns "Some(x)". 
This is an O(n) operation in the worst case, where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.transpose](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#transpose)

Seq.transpose 
transpose 
Returns the transpose of the given sequence of sequences. 
This function returns a sequence that digests the whole initial sequence as soon as
 that sequence is iterated. As a result this function should not be used with
 large or infinite sequences. This is an O(n*m) operation, where n and m are the dimensions.

### [Seq.truncate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#truncate)

Seq.truncate 
truncate 
Returns a sequence that when enumerated returns at most N elements. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(count).

### [Seq.unfold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#unfold)

Seq.unfold 
unfold 
Returns a sequence that contains the elements generated by the given computation.
 The given initial <code>state</code> argument is passed to the element generator.
 For each IEnumerator elements in the stream are generated on-demand by applying the element
 generator, until a None value is returned by the element generator. Each call to the element
 generator returns a new residual <code>state</code>. 
The stream will be recomputed each time an IEnumerator is requested and iterated for the Seq. This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of elements generated.

### [Seq.windowed](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#windowed)

Seq.windowed 
windowed 
Returns a sequence yielding sliding windows containing elements drawn from the input
 sequence. Each window is returned as a fresh array. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequence.

### [Seq.zip](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#zip)

Seq.zip 
zip 
Combines the two sequences into a sequence of pairs. The two sequences need not have equal lengths:
 when one sequence is exhausted any remaining elements in the other
 sequence are ignored. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequences.

### [Seq.zip3](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#zip3)

Seq.zip3 
zip3 
Combines the three sequences into a sequence of triples. The sequences need not have equal lengths:
 when one sequence is exhausted any remaining elements in the other
 sequences are ignored. 
Sequence construction is O(1). Enumeration is O(n), where n is the length of the sequences.

### [Seq.removeAt](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html#removeAt)

removeAt 
Return a new sequence with the item at a given index removed. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the index.

removeManyAt

randomChoiceWith 

 Returns a random element from the given sequence with the specified <code>Random</code> instance.

### [Set.empty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#empty)

empty 
The empty set for the type 'T. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Set.singleton](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#singleton)

Set.singleton 
singleton 
The set containing the given element. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Set.add](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#add)

Set.add 
add 
Returns a new set with an element added to the set. No exception is raised if
 the set already contains the given element. 
This is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.contains](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#contains)

Set.contains 
contains 
Evaluates to "true" if the given element is in the given set. 
This is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.isSubset](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#isSubset)

Set.isSubset 
isSubset 
Evaluates to "true" if all elements of the first set are in the second 
This is an O(m log n) operation, where m is the number of elements in <code>set1</code> and n is the number of elements in <code>set2</code>.

### [Set.isProperSubset](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#isProperSubset)

Set.isProperSubset 
isProperSubset 
Evaluates to "true" if all elements of the first set are in the second, and at least
 one element of the second is not in the first. 
This is an O(m log n) operation, where m is the number of elements in <code>set1</code> and n is the number of elements in <code>set2</code>.

### [Set.isSuperset](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#isSuperset)

Set.isSuperset 
isSuperset 
Evaluates to "true" if all elements of the second set are in the first. 
This is an O(m log n) operation, where m is the number of elements in <code>set2</code> and n is the number of elements in <code>set1</code>.

### [Set.isProperSuperset](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#isProperSuperset)

Set.isProperSuperset 
isProperSuperset 
Evaluates to "true" if all elements of the second set are in the first, and at least
 one element of the first is not in the second. 
This is an O(m log n) operation, where m is the number of elements in <code>set2</code> and n is the number of elements in <code>set1</code>.

### [Set.count](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#count)

Set.count 
count 
Returns the number of elements in the set. Same as <code>size</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation.

### [Set.exists](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#exists)

Set.exists 
exists 
Tests if any element of the collection satisfies the given predicate.
 If the input function is <code>predicate</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code>
 then computes <code>p i0 or ... or p iN</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.filter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#filter)

Set.filter 
filter 
Returns a new collection containing only the elements of the collection
 for which the given predicate returns True. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#map)

Set.map 
map 
Returns a new collection containing the results of applying the
 given function to each element of the input set. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.fold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#fold)

Set.fold 
fold 
Applies the given accumulating function to all the elements of the set 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.foldBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#foldBack)

Set.foldBack 
foldBack 
Applies the given accumulating function to all the elements of the set. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.forall](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#forall)

Set.forall 
forall 
Tests if all elements of the collection satisfy the given predicate.
 If the input function is <code>f</code> and the elements are <code>i0...iN</code> and "j0...jN"
 then computes <code>p i0 && ... && p iN</code>. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.intersect](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#intersect)

Set.intersect 
intersect 
Computes the intersection of the two sets. 
This is an O(m log n) operation, where m is the number of elements in the first set and n is the number of elements in the second set.

### [Set.intersectMany](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#intersectMany)

Set.intersectMany 
intersectMany 
Computes the intersection of a sequence of sets. The sequence must be non-empty. 
This is an O((k-1) * m log n) operation, where k is the number of sets in the sequence, m is the size of each set, and n is the size of the accumulated intersection.

### [Set.union](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#union)

Set.union 
union 
Computes the union of the two sets. 
This is an O(m log n) operation, where m is the number of elements in the first set and n is the number of elements in the second set.

### [Set.unionMany](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#unionMany)

Set.unionMany 
unionMany 
Computes the union of a sequence of sets. 
This is an O(k * m log n) operation, where k is the number of sets in the sequence, m is the average size of each set, and n is the size of the accumulated union.

### [Set.isEmpty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#isEmpty)

Set.isEmpty 
isEmpty 
Returns "true" if the set is empty. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Set.iter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#iter)

Set.iter 
iter 
Applies the given function to each element of the set, in order according
 to the comparison function. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.partition](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#partition)

Set.partition 
partition 
Splits the set into two sets containing the elements for which the given predicate
 returns true and false respectively. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.partitionWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#partitionWith)

Set.partitionWith 
partitionWith 
Splits the set into two sets, by applying the given partitioning function
 to each element. Returns <code>Choice1Of2</code> elements in the first set and
 <code>Choice2Of2</code> elements in the second set. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.remove](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#remove)

Set.remove 
remove 
Returns a new set with the given element removed. No exception is raised if
 the set doesn't contain the given element. 
This is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.minElement](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#minElement)

Set.minElement 
minElement 
Returns the lowest element in the set according to the ordering being used for the set. 
This is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set.maxElement](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#maxElement)

Set.maxElement 
maxElement 
Returns the highest element in the set according to the ordering being used for the set. 
This is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

This is an O(n log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the list.

### [Set.toSeq](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#toSeq)

toSeq

### [Set.ofSeq](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html#ofSeq)

Set.ofSeq 
ofSeq 
Builds a new collection from the given enumerable object. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the sequence.

Set.difference 
difference 
Returns a new set with the elements of the second set removed from the first. 
This is an O(m log n) operation, where m is the number of elements in the second set and n is the number of elements in the first set.

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html)

Map<'Key, 'Value> 
Immutable maps based on binary trees, where keys are ordered by F# generic comparison. By default
 comparison is the F# structural comparison function or uses implementations of the IComparable interface on key values. 
See the <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-mapmodule.html">Map</a> module for further operations on maps.

 All members of this class are thread-safe and may be used concurrently from multiple threads. 
Map<'Key, 'Value>.``.ctor`` 
``.ctor`` 
Map<'Key, 'Value>.Add 
Add 
Map<'Key, 'Value>.Change 
Change 
Map<'Key, 'Value>.ContainsKey 
ContainsKey 
Map<'Key, 'Value>.Remove 
Remove 
Map<'Key, 'Value>.TryFind 
TryFind 
Map<'Key, 'Value>.TryGetValue 
TryGetValue 
Map<'Key, 'Value>.IsEmpty 
IsEmpty 
Map<'Key, 'Value>.Count 
Count 
Map<'Key, 'Value>.Values 
Values 
Map<'Key, 'Value>.Item 
Item 
Map<'Key, 'Value>.Keys 
Keys

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>.``.ctor``](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html#``.ctor``)

Map<'Key, 'Value>.``.ctor`` 
``.ctor`` 
Builds a map that contains the bindings of the given IEnumerable. 
This is an O(n log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the sequence.

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>.Add](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html#Add)

Map<'Key, 'Value>.Add 
Add 
Returns a new map with the binding added to the given map.
 If a binding with the given key already exists in the input map, the existing binding is replaced by the new binding in the result map. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>.Change](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html#Change)

Map<'Key, 'Value>.Change 
Change 
Returns a new map with the value stored under key changed according to f. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>.ContainsKey](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html#ContainsKey)

Map<'Key, 'Value>.ContainsKey 
ContainsKey 
Tests if an element is in the domain of the map. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>.Remove](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html#Remove)

Map<'Key, 'Value>.Remove 
Remove 
Removes an element from the domain of the map. No exception is raised if the element is not present. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>.TryFind](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html#TryFind)

Map<'Key, 'Value>.TryFind 
TryFind 
Lookup an element in the map, returning a <code>Some</code> value if the element is in the domain
 of the map and <code>None</code> if not. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>.TryGetValue](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html#TryGetValue)

Map<'Key, 'Value>.TryGetValue 
TryGetValue 
Lookup an element in the map, assigning to <code>value</code> if the element is in the domain
 of the map and returning <code>false</code> if not. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>.IsEmpty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html#IsEmpty)

Map<'Key, 'Value>.IsEmpty 
IsEmpty 
Returns true if there are no bindings in the map. 
This is an O(1) operation.

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>.Count](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html#Count)

Map<'Key, 'Value>.Count 
Count 
The number of bindings in the map. 
This is an O(n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>.Values](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html#Values)

Map<'Key, 'Value>.Values 
Values 
All the values in the map, including the duplicates.
 The sequence will be ordered by the keys of the map. 
This is an O(n) operation, creating a sequence of all values.

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>.Item](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html#Item)

Map<'Key, 'Value>.Item 
Item 
Lookup an element in the map. Raise <code>KeyNotFoundException</code> if no binding
 exists in the map. 
Maps are represented as binary trees so this is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of bindings in the map.

### [Map<'Key, 'Value>.Keys](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpmap-2.html#Keys)

Map<'Key, 'Value>.Keys 
Keys 
The keys in the map.
 The sequence will be ordered by the keys of the map. 
This is an O(n) operation, creating a sequence of all keys.

### [Set<'T>](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpset-1.html)

Set<'T> 
Immutable sets based on binary trees, where elements are ordered by F# generic comparison. By default
 comparison is the F# structural comparison function or uses implementations of the IComparable interface on element values. 
See the <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-setmodule.html">Set</a> module for further operations on sets.

 All members of this class are thread-safe and may be used concurrently from multiple threads.

Create a set containing elements drawn from the given sequence.

### [Set<'T>.Add](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpset-1.html#Add)

Set<'T>.Add 
Add 
A useful shortcut for Set.add. Note this operation produces a new set
 and does not mutate the original set. The new set will share many storage
 nodes with the original. See the Set module for further operations on sets. 
This is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set<'T>.Contains](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpset-1.html#Contains)

Set<'T>.Contains 
Contains 
A useful shortcut for Set.contains. See the Set module for further operations on sets. 
This is an O(log n) operation, where n is the number of elements in the set.

### [Set<'T>.IsProperSubsetOf](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpset-1.html#IsProperSubsetOf)

Set<'T>.IsProperSubsetOf 
IsProperSubsetOf 
Evaluates to "true" if all elements of the first set are in the second, and at least
 one element of the second is not in the first. 
This is an O(n log m) operation, where n is the number of elements in this set and m is the number of elements in <code>otherSet</code>.

### [Set<'T>.IsProperSupersetOf](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpset-1.html#IsProperSupersetOf)

Set<'T>.IsProperSupersetOf 
IsProperSupersetOf 
Evaluates to "true" if all elements of the second set are in the first, and at least
 one element of the first is not in the second. 
This is an O(m log n) operation, where m is the number of elements in <code>otherSet</code> and n is the number of elements in this set.

### [Set<'T>.IsSubsetOf](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpset-1.html#IsSubsetOf)

Set<'T>.IsSubsetOf 
IsSubsetOf 
Evaluates to "true" if all elements of the first set are in the second. 
This is an O(n log m) operation, where n is the number of elements in this set and m is the number of elements in <code>otherSet</code>.

### [Set<'T>.IsSupersetOf](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-fsharpset-1.html#IsSupersetOf)

Set<'T>.IsSupersetOf 
IsSupersetOf 
Evaluates to "true" if all elements of the second set are in the first. 
This is an O(m log n) operation, where m is the number of elements in <code>otherSet</code> and n is the number of elements in this set.

### ['T list](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-list-1.html)

'T list 
The type of immutable singly-linked lists.  
See the <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-listmodule.html">List</a> module for further operations related to lists.

 Use the constructors <code>[]</code> and <code>::</code> (infix) to create values of this type, or
 the notation <code>[1; 2; 3]</code>. Use the values in the <code>List</code> module to manipulate 
 values of this type, or pattern match against the values directly.

  See also <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fsharp/language-reference/lists">F# Language Guide - Lists</a>.

'T list.Tail 
Tail 
Gets the tail of the list, which is a list containing all the elements of the list, excluding the first element

### ['T list.Item](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-list-1.html#Item)

'T list.Item 
Item 
Gets the element of the list at the given position. 
Lists are represented as linked lists so this is an O(n) operation.

'T list.Empty 
Empty 
Returns an empty list of a particular type

### ['T seq](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seq-1.html)

'T seq 
An abbreviation for the CLI type <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.ienumerable-1">IEnumerable</a> 

  See the <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-collections-seqmodule.html">Seq</a> module for further operations related to sequences.

  See also <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fsharp/language-reference/sequences">F# Language Guide - Sequences</a>.

### [Async](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-asyncmodule.html)

Async 
Contains camelCase module-level functions for <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync-1.html">Async</a> computations.

### [Async.result](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-asyncmodule.html#result)

Async.result 
result 
Creates an asynchronous computation that returns the given value.

### [Async.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-asyncmodule.html#map)

Async.map 
map 
Creates an asynchronous computation that applies the mapping function to the result of the given computation.

### [Async.bind](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-asyncmodule.html#bind)

Async.bind 
bind 
Creates an asynchronous computation that passes the result of the given computation to the binder function.

### [Async.ignore](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-asyncmodule.html#ignore)

Async.ignore 
ignore 
Creates an asynchronous computation that runs the given computation and ignores its result.

### [Async.catchWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-asyncmodule.html#catchWith)

Async.catchWith 
catchWith 
Creates an asynchronous computation that yields the original result on success, or the result of
 <code>handler exn</code> for non-cancellation exceptions. 
<code>OperationCanceledException</code> and derived types such as <code>TaskCanceledException</code> propagate unchanged,
 and therefore are never passed to <code>handler</code>.

### [Async.catch](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-asyncmodule.html#catch)

Async.catch 
catch 
Creates an asynchronous computation that reifies the outcome of the given <code>computation</code> as a <code>Result</code>:
 <code>Ok</code> on success, <code>Error</code> on failure, so exceptions become values. Cancellation still propagates. 
<code>OperationCanceledException</code> and derived types such as <code>TaskCanceledException</code> propagate unchanged.

### [Async.empty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-asyncmodule.html#empty)

Async.empty 
empty 
An asynchronous computation that returns <code>unit</code>. This is equivalent to <code>async.Zero()</code>.

### [AsyncTaskLikeExtensions](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-asynctasklikeextensions.html)

AsyncTaskLikeExtensions 
A module of extension members providing support for awaiting any task-like value via the GetAwaiter pattern. 
AsyncTaskLikeExtensions.Await 
Await 
AsyncTaskLikeExtensions.StartTaskImmediate 
StartTaskImmediate

### [AsyncTaskLikeExtensions.Await](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-asynctasklikeextensions.html#Await)

AsyncTaskLikeExtensions.Await 
Await 
Creates an asynchronous computation that will wait for the given task-like value to complete and return
 its result. 
<p>For the common case where you are running a Task within an Asynchronous Computation,
 see <c>StartTaskImmediate</c>, which surfaces the ambient <c>CancellationToken</c>
 so that it can be passed to the Task being started.</p><p>The value must satisfy the GetAwaiter pattern: it must have a <c>GetAwaiter()</c> method
 returning an awaiter implementing <see cref="T:System.Runtime.CompilerServices.ICriticalNotifyCompletion" />
 with <c>IsCompleted</c> and <c>GetResult()</c> members.</p><p>Exceptions thrown by <c>GetResult()</c> are propagated directly.</p><p>Unlike the <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.Task" />
 and <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.ValueTask" />
 overloads, an <see cref="T:System.AggregateException" /> carrying multiple inner exceptions is not preserved:
 the first inner exception surfaces (standard <c>GetResult()</c> semantics).</p><p>This overload uses statically resolved type parameters (SRTP) so it can accept any task-like type.
 The specific overloads for <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.Task`1" />, <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.Task" />,
 <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.ValueTask`1" /> and <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.ValueTask" />
 are preferred when the argument type is known.</p>

### [AsyncTaskLikeExtensions.StartTaskImmediate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-asynctasklikeextensions.html#StartTaskImmediate)

AsyncTaskLikeExtensions.StartTaskImmediate 
StartTaskImmediate 
Creates an asynchronous computation that passes the ambient <code>Async.CancellationToken</code> to
 <code>createTask</code>, and then awaits the resulting task-like value. 
The value returned by <code>createTask</code> must satisfy the GetAwaiter pattern: it must have a
 <code>GetAwaiter()</code> method returning an awaiter implementing
 <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.runtime.compilerservices.icriticalnotifycompletion">ICriticalNotifyCompletion</a>
 with <code>IsCompleted</code> and <code>GetResult()</code> members.

 This overload uses statically resolved type parameters (SRTP) so it can accept factories returning
 any task-like type, including <code>YieldAwaitable</code> (from <code>Task.Yield()</code>) and
 <code>ConfiguredTaskAwaitable</code> (from <code>task.ConfigureAwait(false)</code>).
 The specific overloads for <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.task-1">Task</a>, <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.task">Task</a>,
 <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.valuetask-1">ValueTask</a> and <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.valuetask">ValueTask</a>
 are preferred when the factory return type is known.

### [CommonExtensions](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-commonextensions.html)

AsyncRead

### [Event](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-eventmodule.html)

### [Event.merge](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-eventmodule.html#merge)

Event.merge 
merge 
Fires the output event when either of the input events fire.

### [Event.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-eventmodule.html#map)

Event.map 
map 
Returns a new event that passes values transformed by the given function.

### [Event.filter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-eventmodule.html#filter)

Event.filter 
filter 
Returns a new event that listens to the original event and triggers the resulting
 event only when the argument to the event passes the given function.

### [Event.partition](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-eventmodule.html#partition)

Event.partition 
partition 
Returns a new event that listens to the original event and triggers the
 first resulting event if the application of the predicate to the event arguments
 returned true, and the second event if it returned false.

### [Event.split](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-eventmodule.html#split)

Event.split 
split 
Returns a new event that listens to the original event and triggers the
 first resulting event if the application of the function to the event arguments
 returned a Choice1Of2, and the second event if it returns a Choice2Of2.

### [Event.choose](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-eventmodule.html#choose)

Event.choose 
choose 
Returns a new event which fires on a selection of messages from the original event.
 The selection function takes an original message to an optional new message.

### [Event.scan](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-eventmodule.html#scan)

Event.scan 
scan 
Returns a new event consisting of the results of applying the given accumulating function
 to successive values triggered on the input event.  An item of internal state
 records the current value of the state parameter.  The internal state is not locked during the
 execution of the accumulation function, so care should be taken that the
 input IEvent not triggered by multiple threads simultaneously.

### [Event.add](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-eventmodule.html#add)

Event.add 
add 
Runs the given function each time the given event is triggered.

### [Event.pairwise](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-eventmodule.html#pairwise)

Event.pairwise 
pairwise 
Returns a new event that triggers on the second and subsequent triggerings of the input event.
 The Nth triggering of the input event passes the arguments from the N-1th and Nth triggering as
 a pair. The argument passed to the N-1th triggering is held in hidden internal state until the
 Nth triggering occurs.

 prevent other threads also computing the value.

### [Observable](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-observablemodule.html)

Observable 
Contains operations for working with first class event and other observable objects. 
Observable.merge 
merge 
Observable.map 
map 
Observable.filter 
filter 
Observable.partition 
partition 
Observable.split 
split 
Observable.choose 
choose 
Observable.scan 
scan 
Observable.add 
add 
Observable.subscribe 
subscribe 
Observable.pairwise 
pairwise

### [Observable.merge](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-observablemodule.html#merge)

Observable.merge 
merge 
Returns an observable for the merged observations from the sources.
 The returned object propagates success and error values arising
 from either source and completes when both the sources have completed. 
For each observer, the registered intermediate observing object is not
 thread safe. That is, observations arising from the sources must not
 be triggered concurrently on different threads.

### [Observable.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-observablemodule.html#map)

Observable.map 
map 
Returns an observable which transforms the observations of the source by the
 given function. The transformation function is executed once for each
 subscribed observer. The returned object also propagates error observations
 arising from the source and completes when the source completes.

### [Observable.filter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-observablemodule.html#filter)

Observable.filter 
filter 
Returns an observable which filters the observations of the source
 by the given function. The observable will see only those observations
 for which the predicate returns true. The predicate is executed once for
 each subscribed observer. The returned object also propagates error
 observations arising from the source and completes when the source completes.

### [Observable.partition](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-observablemodule.html#partition)

Observable.partition 
partition 
Returns two observables which partition the observations of the source by
 the given function. The first will trigger observations for those values
 for which the predicate returns true. The second will trigger observations
 for those values where the predicate returns false. The predicate is
 executed once for each subscribed observer. Both also propagate all error
 observations arising from the source and each completes when the source
 completes.

### [Observable.split](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-observablemodule.html#split)

Observable.split 
split 
Returns two observables which split the observations of the source by the
 given function. The first will trigger observations <code>x</code> for which the
 splitter returns <code>Choice1Of2 x</code>. The second will trigger observations
 <code>y</code> for which the splitter returns <code>Choice2Of2 y</code> The splitter is
 executed once for each subscribed observer. Both also propagate error
 observations arising from the source and each completes when the source
 completes.

### [Observable.choose](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-observablemodule.html#choose)

Observable.choose 
choose 
Returns an observable which chooses a projection of observations from the source
 using the given function. The returned object will trigger observations <code>x</code>
 for which the splitter returns <code>Some x</code>. The returned object also propagates
 all errors arising from the source and completes when the source completes.

### [Observable.scan](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-observablemodule.html#scan)

Observable.scan 
scan 
Returns an observable which, for each observer, allocates an item of state
 and applies the given accumulating function to successive values arising from
 the input. The returned object will trigger observations for each computed
 state value, excluding the initial value. The returned object propagates
 all errors arising from the source and completes when the source completes. 
For each observer, the registered intermediate observing object is not thread safe.
 That is, observations arising from the source must not be triggered concurrently
 on different threads.

### [Observable.add](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-observablemodule.html#add)

Observable.add 
add 
Creates an observer which permanently subscribes to the given observable and which calls
 the given function for each observation.

### [Observable.subscribe](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-observablemodule.html#subscribe)

Observable.subscribe 
subscribe 
Creates an observer which subscribes to the given observable and which calls
 the given function for each observation.

### [Observable.pairwise](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-observablemodule.html#pairwise)

Observable.pairwise 
pairwise 
Returns a new observable that triggers on the second and subsequent triggerings of the input observable.
 The Nth triggering of the input observable passes the arguments from the N-1th and Nth triggering as
 a pair. The argument passed to the N-1th triggering is held in hidden internal state until the
 Nth triggering occurs. 
For each observer, the registered intermediate observing object is not thread safe.
 That is, observations arising from the source must not be triggered concurrently
 on different threads.

### [Task](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-taskmodule.html)

Task
