### [Task.result](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-taskmodule.html#result)

Task.result 
result 
Creates a task that returns the given value.

### [Task.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-taskmodule.html#map)

Task.map 
map 
Creates a task that applies the mapping function to the result of the given task.

### [Task.bind](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-taskmodule.html#bind)

Task.bind 
bind 
Creates a task that passes the result of the given task to the binder function.

### [Task.ignore](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-taskmodule.html#ignore)

Task.ignore 
ignore 
Creates a task that runs the given task and ignores its result.

### [Task.catchWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-taskmodule.html#catchWith)

Task.catchWith 
catchWith 
Creates a <code>Task</code> that yields the original result on success, or the result of
 <code>handler exn</code> for non-cancellation exceptions. 
<code>OperationCanceledException</code> and derived types such as <code>TaskCanceledException</code> propagate unchanged
 (and the task remains Canceled) in order to maintain cancellation semantics, and therefore are never passed to <code>handler</code>.

### [Task.catch](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-taskmodule.html#catch)

Task.catch 
catch 
Creates a <code>Task</code> that reifies the outcome of the given <code>Task</code> as a <code>Result</code>:
 <code>Ok</code> on success, <code>Error</code> on failure, so faults become values. Cancellation still propagates. 
<code>OperationCanceledException</code> and derived types such as <code>TaskCanceledException</code> propagate unchanged
 (and the task remains Canceled) in order to maintain cancellation semantics.

### [Task.empty](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-taskmodule.html#empty)

Task.empty 
empty 
A completed task that returns <code>unit</code>. This is a <code>Task<unit></code> (not the non-generic <code>Task.CompletedTask</code>).

### [Task.ofValueTask](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-taskmodule.html#ofValueTask)

Task.ofValueTask 
ofValueTask 
Converts a <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.valuetask-1">ValueTask</a> to a <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.task-1">Task</a>.

### [TaskBuilder](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-taskbuildermodule.html)

TaskBuilder 
 Contains the `task` computation expression builder.

### [TaskBuilder.task](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-taskbuildermodule.html#task)

TaskBuilder.task 
task 

 Builds a task using computation expression syntax.

### [TaskBuilder.backgroundTask](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-taskbuildermodule.html#backgroundTask)

TaskBuilder.backgroundTask 
backgroundTask 

 Builds a task using computation expression syntax which switches to execute on a background thread if not
 already doing so.
  

 If the task is created on a foreground thread (where <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.synchronizationcontext.current">SynchronizationContext.Current</a> is non-null)
 its body is executed on a background thread using <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.task.run">Task.Run</a>.
 If created on a background thread (where <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.synchronizationcontext.current">SynchronizationContext.Current</a> is null) it is executed
 immediately on that thread.

 <code>Ok</code> on success, <code>Error</code> on failure, so faults become values. Cancellation still propagates.

### [WebExtensions.AsyncGetResponse](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-webextensions.html#AsyncGetResponse)

WebExtensions.AsyncGetResponse 
AsyncGetResponse 
Returns an asynchronous computation that, when run, will wait for a response to the given WebRequest.

### [Async<'T>](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync-1.html)

Async<'T> 

 An asynchronous computation, which, when run, will eventually produce a value  of type T, or else raises an exception.
  

  This type has no members. Asynchronous computations are normally specified either by using an async expression
  or the static methods in the <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync-1.html">Async</a> type.

  See also <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fsharp/language-reference/async-expressions">F# Language Guide - Async Workflows</a>.

### [Async](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html)

  See also <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fsharp/language-reference/async-expressions">F# Language Guide - Async Workflows</a>.

### [Async.AsBeginEnd](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#AsBeginEnd)

Async.AsBeginEnd 
AsBeginEnd 
Creates three functions that can be used to implement the .NET 1.0 Asynchronous 
 Programming Model (APM) for a given asynchronous computation.

### [Async.Await](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Await)

Async.Await 
Await 
Creates an asynchronous computation that will wait for the given <code>ValueTask</code> to complete. 
<p>Exceptions are surfaced directly: a task faulted with a single exception raises that
 exception; only <see cref="T:System.AggregateException" />s carrying multiple inner exceptions are
 re-raised as-is. For the legacy behavior of uniformly presenting the raw underlying
 <see cref="T:System.AggregateException" />, use <c>Async.AwaitTask</c>.</p><p>If the task is canceled then <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException" /> is raised.</p><p>Note the task may be governed by a different cancellation token than the overall async computation;
 typically tasks should be wired to the ambient cancellation token obtained via
 <c>let! ct = Async.CancellationToken</c>, catching <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException" />
 where the overall async is started.</p><p>For the common case where you are running a Task within an Asynchronous Computation,
 see <c>StartTaskImmediate</c>, which surfaces the ambient <c>CancellationToken</c>
 so that it can be passed to the Task being started.</p>

### [Async.Await](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Await)

Async.Await 
Await 
Creates an asynchronous computation that will wait for the given <code>ValueTask</code> to complete and return
 its result. 
<p>Exceptions are surfaced directly: a task faulted with a single exception raises that
 exception; only <see cref="T:System.AggregateException" />s carrying multiple inner exceptions are
 re-raised as-is. For the legacy behavior of uniformly presenting the raw underlying
 <see cref="T:System.AggregateException" />, use <c>Async.AwaitTask</c>.</p><p>If the task is canceled then <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException" /> is raised.</p><p>Note the task may be governed by a different cancellation token than the overall async computation;
 typically tasks should be wired to the ambient cancellation token obtained via
 <c>let! ct = Async.CancellationToken</c>, catching <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException" />
 where the overall async is started.</p><p>For the common case where you are running a Task within an Asynchronous Computation,
 see <c>StartTaskImmediate</c>, which surfaces the ambient <c>CancellationToken</c>
 so that it can be passed to the Task being started.</p>

### [Async.Await](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Await)

Async.Await 
Await 
Creates an asynchronous computation that will wait for the given task to complete. 
<p>Exceptions are surfaced directly: a task faulted with a single exception raises that
 exception; only <see cref="T:System.AggregateException" />s carrying multiple inner exceptions are
 re-raised as-is. For the legacy behavior of uniformly presenting the raw underlying
 <see cref="T:System.AggregateException" />, use <c>Async.AwaitTask</c>.</p><p>If the task is canceled then <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException" /> is raised.</p><p>Note the task may be governed by a different cancellation token than the overall async computation;
 typically tasks should be wired to the ambient cancellation token obtained via
 <c>let! ct = Async.CancellationToken</c>, catching <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException" />
 where the overall async is started.</p><p>For the common case where you are running a Task within an Asynchronous Computation,
 see <c>StartTaskImmediate</c>, which surfaces the ambient <c>CancellationToken</c>
 so that it can be passed to the Task being started.</p>

### [Async.Await](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Await)

Async.Await 
Await 
Creates an asynchronous computation that will wait for the given task to complete and return
 its result. 
<p>Exceptions are surfaced directly: a task faulted with a single exception raises that
 exception; only <see cref="T:System.AggregateException" />s carrying multiple inner exceptions are
 re-raised as-is. For the legacy behavior of uniformly presenting the raw underlying
 <see cref="T:System.AggregateException" />, use <c>Async.AwaitTask</c>.</p><p>If the task is canceled then <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException" /> is raised.</p><p>Note the task may be governed by a different cancellation token than the overall async computation;
 typically tasks should be wired to the ambient cancellation token obtained via
 <c>let! ct = Async.CancellationToken</c>, catching <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException" />
 where the overall async is started.</p><p>For the common case where you are running a Task within an Asynchronous Computation,
 see <c>StartTaskImmediate</c>, which surfaces the ambient <c>CancellationToken</c>
 so that it can be passed to the Task being started.</p>

### [Async.AwaitEvent](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#AwaitEvent)

Async.AwaitEvent 
AwaitEvent 
Creates an asynchronous computation that waits for a single invocation of a CLI 
 event by adding a handler to the event. Once the computation completes or is 
 cancelled, the handler is removed from the event. 
The computation will respond to cancellation while waiting for the event. If a 
 cancellation occurs, and <code>cancelAction</code> is specified, then it is executed, and 
 the computation continues to wait for the event.

 If <code>cancelAction</code> is not specified, then cancellation causes the computation
 to cancel immediately.

### [Async.AwaitIAsyncResult](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#AwaitIAsyncResult)

Async.AwaitIAsyncResult 
AwaitIAsyncResult 
Creates an asynchronous computation that will wait on the IAsyncResult. 
The computation returns true if the handle indicated a result within the given timeout.

### [Async.AwaitTask](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#AwaitTask)

Async.AwaitTask 
AwaitTask 
Creates an asynchronous computation that will wait asynchronously for the given task to complete.
 Note exceptions are wrapped in <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.aggregateexception">AggregateException</a>; for new
 code, prefer <code>Async.Await</code>, which surfaces single exceptions directly. 
<p>If the task is canceled then <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException" /> is raised. Note
 that the task may be governed by a different cancellation token to the overall async computation
 where the AwaitTask occurs. In practice you should normally start the task with the
 cancellation token returned by <c>let! ct = Async.CancellationToken</c>, and catch
 any <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException" /> at the point where the
 overall async is started.</p><p>For the common case where you are running a Task within an Asynchronous Computation,
 see <c>StartTaskImmediate</c>, which surfaces the ambient <c>CancellationToken</c>
 so that it can be passed to the Task being started.</p>

### [Async.AwaitTask](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#AwaitTask)

Async.AwaitTask 
AwaitTask 
Creates an asynchronous computation that will wait asynchronously for the given task to complete, returning
 its result. Note exceptions are wrapped in <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.aggregateexception">AggregateException</a>; for new
 code, prefer <code>Async.Await</code>, which surfaces single exceptions directly. 
<p>If the task is canceled then <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException" /> is raised. Note
 that the task may be governed by a different cancellation token to the overall async computation
 where the AwaitTask occurs. In practice you should normally start the task with the
 cancellation token returned by <c>let! ct = Async.CancellationToken</c>, and catch
 any <see cref="T:System.Threading.Tasks.TaskCanceledException" /> at the point where the
 overall async is started.</p><p>For the common case where you are running a Task within an Asynchronous Computation,
 see <c>StartTaskImmediate</c>, which surfaces the ambient <c>CancellationToken</c>
 so that it can be passed to the Task being started.</p>

### [Async.AwaitWaitHandle](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#AwaitWaitHandle)

Async.AwaitWaitHandle 
AwaitWaitHandle 
Creates an asynchronous computation that will wait on the given WaitHandle. 
The computation returns true if the handle indicated a result within the given timeout.

### [Async.CancelDefaultToken](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#CancelDefaultToken)

Async.CancelDefaultToken 
CancelDefaultToken 
Raises the cancellation condition for the most recent set of asynchronous computations started 
 without any specific CancellationToken. Replaces the global CancellationTokenSource with a new 
 global token source for any asynchronous computations created after this point without any 
 specific CancellationToken.

### [Async.Catch](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Catch)

Async.Catch 
Catch 
Creates an asynchronous computation that executes <code>computation</code>.
 If this computation completes successfully then return <code>Choice1Of2</code> with the returned
 value. If this computation raises an exception before it completes then return <code>Choice2Of2</code>
 with the raised exception.

### [Async.Choice](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Choice)

Async.Choice 
Choice 

 Creates an asynchronous computation that executes all given asynchronous computations in parallel, 
 returning the result of the first succeeding computation (one whose result is 'Some x').
 If all child computations complete with None, the parent computation also returns None.
  

 If any child computation raises an exception, then the overall computation will trigger an 
 exception, and cancel the others. 

 The overall computation will respond to cancellation while executing the child computations.
 If cancelled, the computation will cancel any remaining child computations but will still wait
 for the other child computations to complete.

### [Async.FromBeginEnd](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#FromBeginEnd)

Async.FromBeginEnd 
FromBeginEnd 
Creates an asynchronous computation in terms of a Begin/End pair of actions in 
 the style used in .NET 2.0 APIs. 
The computation will respond to cancellation while waiting for the completion
 of the operation. If a cancellation occurs, and <code>cancelAction</code> is specified, then it is 
 executed, and the computation continues to wait for the completion of the operation.

 If <code>cancelAction</code> is not specified, then cancellation causes the computation
 to stop immediately, and subsequent invocations of the callback are ignored.

### [Async.FromBeginEnd](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#FromBeginEnd)

Async.FromBeginEnd 
FromBeginEnd 

 Creates an asynchronous computation in terms of a Begin/End pair of actions in 
 the style used in .NET 2.0 APIs. 
The computation will respond to cancellation while waiting for the completion
 of the operation. If a cancellation occurs, and <code>cancelAction</code> is specified, then it is 
 executed, and the computation continues to wait for the completion of the operation.

 If <code>cancelAction</code> is not specified, then cancellation causes the computation
 to stop immediately, and subsequent invocations of the callback are ignored.

### [Async.FromBeginEnd](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#FromBeginEnd)

Async.FromBeginEnd 
FromBeginEnd 

  Creates an asynchronous computation in terms of a Begin/End pair of actions in 
  the style used in .NET 2.0 APIs.
  
The computation will respond to cancellation while waiting for the completion
 of the operation. If a cancellation occurs, and <code>cancelAction</code> is specified, then it is 
 executed, and the computation continues to wait for the completion of the operation.

  If <code>cancelAction</code> is not specified, then cancellation causes the computation
  to stop immediately, and subsequent invocations of the callback are ignored.

### [Async.FromBeginEnd](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#FromBeginEnd)

Async.FromBeginEnd 
FromBeginEnd 

  Creates an asynchronous computation in terms of a Begin/End pair of actions in 
  the style used in CLI APIs.
  

 The computation will respond to cancellation while waiting for the completion
 of the operation. If a cancellation occurs, and <code>cancelAction</code> is specified, then it is 
 executed, and the computation continues to wait for the completion of the operation.

 If <code>cancelAction</code> is not specified, then cancellation causes the computation
 to stop immediately, and subsequent invocations of the callback are ignored.

### [Async.FromContinuations](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#FromContinuations)

Async.FromContinuations 
FromContinuations 
Creates an asynchronous computation that captures the current
 success, exception and cancellation continuations. The callback must 
 eventually call exactly one of the given continuations.

### [Async.Ignore](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Ignore)

Async.Ignore 
Ignore 
Creates an asynchronous computation that runs the given computation and ignores 
 its result.

### [Async.OnCancel](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#OnCancel)

Async.OnCancel 
OnCancel 
Generates a scoped, cooperative cancellation handler for use within an asynchronous workflow. 
For example,
     <code>async { use! holder = Async.OnCancel interruption ... }</code> 
 generates an asynchronous computation where, if a cancellation happens any time during 
 the execution of the asynchronous computation in the scope of <code>holder</code>, then action 
 <code>interruption</code> is executed on the thread that is performing the cancellation. This can 
 be used to arrange for a computation to be asynchronously notified that a cancellation 
 has occurred, e.g. by setting a flag, or deregistering a pending I/O action.

### [Async.Parallel](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Parallel)

Async.Parallel 
Parallel 
Creates an asynchronous computation that executes all the given asynchronous computations,
 initially queueing each as work items and using a fork/join pattern. 
If all child computations succeed, an array of results is passed to the success continuation.

 If any child computation raises an exception, then the overall computation will trigger an
 exception, and cancel the others.

 The overall computation will respond to cancellation while executing the child computations.
 If cancelled, the computation will cancel any remaining child computations but will still wait
 for the other child computations to complete.

### [Async.Parallel](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Parallel)

Async.Parallel 
Parallel 
Creates an asynchronous computation that executes all the given asynchronous computations, 
 initially queueing each as work items and using a fork/join pattern. 
If all child computations succeed, an array of results is passed to the success continuation.

 If any child computation raises an exception, then the overall computation will trigger an 
 exception, and cancel the others. 

 The overall computation will respond to cancellation while executing the child computations.
 If cancelled, the computation will cancel any remaining child computations but will still wait
 for the other child computations to complete.

### [Async.RunSynchronously](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#RunSynchronously)

Async.RunSynchronously 
RunSynchronously 
<p>Runs the computation and blocks the caller until it completes.</p><p>Runs inline on the calling thread when it is a thread-pool thread with no ambient SynchronizationContext
 and no timeout; otherwise runs on the thread pool.</p> 
<p>Note For F# interactive, F# scripts, and unit tests consider using
 <see cref="M:Microsoft.FSharp.Control.FSharpAsync.RunSynchronouslyImmediate`1" />, which
 always starts on the calling thread and presents a simpler stack trace in exception cases and/or under a debugger.</p><p>Computation runs directly on the calling thread when
 <see cref="P:System.Threading.SynchronizationContext.Current" /> is <c>null</c>,
 <see cref="P:System.Threading.Thread.IsThreadPoolThread" /> is <c>true</c>, and no timeout is specified.</p>

### [Async.RunSynchronouslyImmediate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#RunSynchronouslyImmediate)

Async.RunSynchronouslyImmediate 
RunSynchronouslyImmediate 
<p>Starts the asynchronous computation on the calling thread, disregarding the ambient
 <see cref="T:System.Threading.SynchronizationContext" />.</p><p>During any asynchronous continuations after the first suspension, the calling thread blocks awaiting the outcome.</p> 
<p>Warning: blocks the calling thread for the duration of the computation. Calling it
 from a UI thread will make the UI unresponsive and risks deadlock if any continuation in the
 computation needs to be dispatched back to that context.</p><p>Normally preferred to <see cref="M:Microsoft.FSharp.Control.FSharpAsync.RunSynchronously`1" /> for
 interactive use in F# scripts and F# interactive (FSI), and for unit tests as: <br />
 - a breakpoint will show a clearer call stack prior to the first suspension (as opposed to it waiting for an asynchronous completion notification from another thread<br />
 - the stack trace in the case of an exception will have two fewer frames.
 </p><p>Does not support a timeout; see
 <see cref="M:Microsoft.FSharp.Control.FSharpAsync.RunSynchronously`1" /> if one is desired.</p><p>Does not ensure execution takes place on a threadpool thread; see
 <see cref="M:Microsoft.FSharp.Control.FSharpAsync.RunSynchronously`1" /> or
 <see cref="M:Microsoft.FSharp.Control.FSharpAsync.SwitchToThreadPool" /> if this is required.</p>

### [Async.Sequential](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Sequential)

Async.Sequential 
Sequential 
Creates an asynchronous computation that executes all the given asynchronous computations sequentially. 
If all child computations succeed, an array of results is passed to the success continuation.

 If any child computation raises an exception, then the overall computation will trigger an
 exception, and cancel the others.

 The overall computation will respond to cancellation while executing the child computations.
 If cancelled, the computation will cancel any remaining child computations but will still wait
 for the other child computations to complete.

Sleep 

  Creates an asynchronous computation that will sleep for the given time. This is scheduled
  using a System.Threading.Timer object. The operation will not block operating system threads
  for the duration of the wait.

  using a System.Threading.Timer object. The operation will not block operating system threads
  for the duration of the wait.

### [Async.StartChild](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#StartChild)

Async.StartChild 
StartChild 
Starts a child computation within an asynchronous workflow. 
 This allows multiple asynchronous computations to be executed simultaneously. 
This method should normally be used as the immediate 
 right-hand-side of a <code>let!</code> binding in an F# asynchronous workflow, that is,
 <pre class="fssnip highlighted"><code lang="fsharp">     <span data-fsdocs-tip="fs1" data-fsdocs-tip-unique="1" class="id">async</span> <span class="pn">{</span> <span class="o">..</span><span class="pn">.</span>
            <span class="k">let!</span> <span class="id">completor1</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="id">childComputation1</span> <span class="o">|></span> <span data-fsdocs-tip="fs2" data-fsdocs-tip-unique="2" class="id">Async</span><span class="pn">.</span><span data-fsdocs-tip="fs3" data-fsdocs-tip-unique="3" class="id">StartChild</span>  
            <span class="k">let!</span> <span class="id">completor2</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="id">childComputation2</span> <span class="o">|></span> <span data-fsdocs-tip="fs2" data-fsdocs-tip-unique="4" class="id">Async</span><span class="pn">.</span><span data-fsdocs-tip="fs3" data-fsdocs-tip-unique="5" class="id">StartChild</span>  
            <span class="o">..</span><span class="pn">.</span> 
            <span class="k">let!</span> <span class="id">result1</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="id">completor1</span> 
            <span class="k">let!</span> <span class="id">result2</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="id">completor2</span> 
            <span class="o">..</span><span class="pn">.</span> <span class="pn">}</span>
</code></pre>
<div popover class="fsdocs-tip" id="fs1">val async: AsyncBuilder</div>
<div popover class="fsdocs-tip" id="fs2">Multiple items<br />type Async =
  static member AsBeginEnd: computation: ('Arg -> Async<'T>) -> ('Arg * AsyncCallback * objnull -> IAsyncResult) * (IAsyncResult -> 'T) * (IAsyncResult -> unit)
  static member AwaitEvent: event: IEvent<'Del,'T> * ?cancelAction: (unit -> unit) -> Async<'T> (requires delegate and 'Del :> Delegate and 'Del: not null)
  static member AwaitIAsyncResult: iar: IAsyncResult * ?millisecondsTimeout: int -> Async<bool>
  static member AwaitTask: task: Task<'T> -> Async<'T> + 1 overload
  static member AwaitWaitHandle: waitHandle: WaitHandle * ?millisecondsTimeout: int -> Async<bool>
  static member CancelDefaultToken: unit -> unit
  static member Catch: computation: Async<'T> -> Async<Choice<'T,exn>>
  static member Choice: computations: Async<'T option> seq -> Async<'T option>
  static member FromBeginEnd: beginAction: (AsyncCallback * objnull -> IAsyncResult) * endAction: (IAsyncResult -> 'T) * ?cancelAction: (unit -> unit) -> Async<'T> + 3 overloads
  static member FromContinuations: callback: (('T -> unit) * (exn -> unit) * (OperationCanceledException -> unit) -> unit) -> Async<'T>
  ...<br /><br />--------------------<br />type Async<'T></div>
<div popover class="fsdocs-tip" id="fs3">static member Async.StartChild: computation: Async<'T> * ?millisecondsTimeout: int -> Async<Async<'T>></div>


 When used in this way, each use of <code>StartChild</code> starts an instance of <code>childComputation</code> 
 and returns a completor object representing a computation to wait for the completion of the operation.
 When executed, the completor awaits the completion of <code>childComputation</code>.

### [Async.StartChildAsTask](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#StartChildAsTask)

Async.StartChildAsTask 
StartChildAsTask 
Creates an asynchronous computation which starts the given computation as a <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.task-1">Task</a>

### [Async.StartImmediate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#StartImmediate)

Async.StartImmediate 
StartImmediate 
Runs an asynchronous computation, starting immediately on the current operating system
 thread. 
If no cancellation token is provided then the default cancellation token is used.

### [Async.StartImmediateAsTask](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#StartImmediateAsTask)

Async.StartImmediateAsTask 
StartImmediateAsTask 
Runs an asynchronous computation, starting immediately on the current operating system
 thread, but also returns the execution as <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.task-1">Task</a> 
If no cancellation token is provided then the default cancellation token is used.
 You may prefer using this method if you want to achieve a similar behavior to async await in C# as 
 async computation starts on the current thread with an ability to return a result.

### [Async.StartTaskImmediate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#StartTaskImmediate)

Async.StartTaskImmediate 
StartTaskImmediate 
Creates an asynchronous computation that passes the ambient <code>Async.CancellationToken</code> to
 <code>createTask</code>, and then awaits the resulting <code>ValueTask</code>. 
The cancellation token of the enclosing async computation is automatically passed to
 <code>createTask</code>, propagating cancellation naturally to the task without requiring manual token capture.

 The resulting task is awaited using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Await">Async.Await</a>;
 exception unwrapping and cancellation handling are as per that overload.

### [Async.StartTaskImmediate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#StartTaskImmediate)

Async.StartTaskImmediate 
StartTaskImmediate 
Creates an asynchronous computation that passes the ambient <code>Async.CancellationToken</code> to
 <code>createTask</code>, and then awaits the resulting <code>ValueTask</code>, returning its result. 
The cancellation token of the enclosing async computation is automatically passed to
 <code>createTask</code>, propagating cancellation naturally to the task without requiring manual token capture.

 The resulting task is awaited using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Await">Async.Await</a>;
 exception unwrapping and cancellation handling are as per that overload.

### [Async.StartTaskImmediate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#StartTaskImmediate)

Async.StartTaskImmediate 
StartTaskImmediate 
Creates an asynchronous computation that passes the ambient <code>Async.CancellationToken</code> to
 <code>createTask</code>, and then awaits the resulting task. 
The cancellation token of the enclosing async computation is automatically passed to
 <code>createTask</code>, propagating cancellation naturally to the task without requiring manual token capture.

 The resulting task is awaited using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Await">Async.Await</a>;
 exception unwrapping and cancellation handling are as per that overload.

### [Async.StartTaskImmediate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#StartTaskImmediate)

Async.StartTaskImmediate 
StartTaskImmediate 
Creates an asynchronous computation that passes the ambient <code>Async.CancellationToken</code> to
 <code>createTask</code>, and then awaits the resulting task, returning its result. 
The cancellation token of the enclosing async computation is automatically passed to
 <code>createTask</code>, propagating cancellation naturally to the task without requiring manual token capture.

 The resulting task is awaited using <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#Await">Async.Await</a>;
 exception unwrapping and cancellation handling are as per that overload.

### [Async.StartWithContinuations](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#StartWithContinuations)

Async.StartWithContinuations 
StartWithContinuations 
Runs an asynchronous computation, starting immediately on the current operating system
 thread. Call one of the three continuations when the operation completes. 
If no cancellation token is provided then the default cancellation token
 is used.

### [Async.SwitchToContext](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#SwitchToContext)

Async.SwitchToContext 
SwitchToContext 
Creates an asynchronous computation that runs
 its continuation using syncContext.Post. If syncContext is null 
 then the asynchronous computation is equivalent to SwitchToThreadPool().

### [Async.SwitchToNewThread](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#SwitchToNewThread)

Async.SwitchToNewThread 
SwitchToNewThread 
Creates an asynchronous computation that creates a new thread and runs
 its continuation in that thread.

### [Async.SwitchToThreadPool](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#SwitchToThreadPool)

Async.SwitchToThreadPool 
SwitchToThreadPool 
Creates an asynchronous computation that queues a work item that runs
 its continuation.

### [Async.TryCancelled](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#TryCancelled)

Async.TryCancelled 
TryCancelled 
Creates an asynchronous computation that executes <code>computation</code>.
 If this computation is cancelled before it completes then the computation generated by 
 running <code>compensation</code> is executed.

### [Async.DefaultCancellationToken](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#DefaultCancellationToken)

Async.DefaultCancellationToken 
DefaultCancellationToken 
Gets the default cancellation token for executing asynchronous computations.

### [Async.CancellationToken](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasync.html#CancellationToken)

Async.CancellationToken 
CancellationToken 
Creates an asynchronous computation that returns the CancellationToken governing the execution 
 of the computation. 
In <code>async { let! token = Async.CancellationToken ...}</code> token can be used to initiate other 
 asynchronous operations that will cancel cooperatively with this workflow.

### [AsyncBuilder](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncbuilder.html)

AsyncBuilder 
The type of the <code>async</code> operator, used to build workflows for asynchronous computations. 
AsyncBuilder.Bind 
Bind 
AsyncBuilder.Combine 
Combine 
AsyncBuilder.Delay 
Delay 
AsyncBuilder.For 
For 
AsyncBuilder.Return 
Return 
AsyncBuilder.ReturnFrom 
ReturnFrom 
AsyncBuilder.TryFinally 
TryFinally 
AsyncBuilder.TryWith 
TryWith 
AsyncBuilder.Using 
Using 
AsyncBuilder.While 
While 
AsyncBuilder.Zero 
Zero

### [AsyncBuilder.Bind](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncbuilder.html#Bind)

AsyncBuilder.Bind 
Bind 
Creates an asynchronous computation that runs <code>computation</code>, and when 
 <code>computation</code> generates a result <code>T</code>, runs <code>binder res</code>. 
A cancellation check is performed when the computation is executed.

 The existence of this method permits the use of <code>let!</code> in the 
 <code>async { ... }</code> computation expression syntax.

### [AsyncBuilder.Combine](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncbuilder.html#Combine)

AsyncBuilder.Combine 
Combine 
Creates an asynchronous computation that first runs <code>computation1</code>
 and then runs <code>computation2</code>, returning the result of <code>computation2</code>. 
A cancellation check is performed when the computation is executed.

 The existence of this method permits the use of expression sequencing in the 
 <code>async { ... }</code> computation expression syntax.

### [AsyncBuilder.Delay](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncbuilder.html#Delay)

AsyncBuilder.Delay 
Delay 
Creates an asynchronous computation that runs <code>generator</code>. 
A cancellation check is performed when the computation is executed.

### [AsyncBuilder.For](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncbuilder.html#For)

AsyncBuilder.For 
For 
Creates an asynchronous computation that enumerates the sequence <code>seq</code>
 on demand and runs <code>body</code> for each element. 
A cancellation check is performed on each iteration of the loop.

 The existence of this method permits the use of <code>for</code> in the 
 <code>async { ... }</code> computation expression syntax.

### [AsyncBuilder.Return](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncbuilder.html#Return)

AsyncBuilder.Return 
Return 
Creates an asynchronous computation that returns the result <code>v</code>. 
A cancellation check is performed when the computation is executed.

 The existence of this method permits the use of <code>return</code> in the 
 <code>async { ... }</code> computation expression syntax.

### [AsyncBuilder.ReturnFrom](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncbuilder.html#ReturnFrom)

AsyncBuilder.ReturnFrom 
ReturnFrom 
Delegates to the input computation. 
The existence of this method permits the use of <code>return!</code> in the 
 <code>async { ... }</code> computation expression syntax.

### [AsyncBuilder.TryFinally](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncbuilder.html#TryFinally)

AsyncBuilder.TryFinally 
TryFinally 
Creates an asynchronous computation that runs <code>computation</code>. The action <code>compensation</code> is executed 
 after <code>computation</code> completes, whether <code>computation</code> exits normally or by an exception. If <code>compensation</code> raises an exception itself
 the original exception is discarded and the new exception becomes the overall result of the computation. 
A cancellation check is performed when the computation is executed.

 The existence of this method permits the use of <code>try/finally</code> in the 
 <code>async { ... }</code> computation expression syntax.

### [AsyncBuilder.TryWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncbuilder.html#TryWith)

AsyncBuilder.TryWith 
TryWith 
Creates an asynchronous computation that runs <code>computation</code> and returns its result.
 If an exception happens then <code>catchHandler(exn)</code> is called and the resulting computation executed instead. 
A cancellation check is performed when the computation is executed.

 The existence of this method permits the use of <code>try/with</code> in the 
 <code>async { ... }</code> computation expression syntax.

### [AsyncBuilder.Using](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncbuilder.html#Using)

AsyncBuilder.Using 
Using 
Creates an asynchronous computation that runs <code>binder(resource)</code>. 
 The action <code>resource.Dispose()</code> is executed as this computation yields its result
 or if the asynchronous computation exits by an exception or by cancellation. 
A cancellation check is performed when the computation is executed.

 The existence of this method permits the use of <code>use</code> and <code>use!</code> in the 
 <code>async { ... }</code> computation expression syntax.

### [AsyncBuilder.While](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncbuilder.html#While)

AsyncBuilder.While 
While 
Creates an asynchronous computation that runs <code>computation</code> repeatedly 
 until <code>guard()</code> becomes false. 
A cancellation check is performed whenever the computation is executed.

 The existence of this method permits the use of <code>while</code> in the 
 <code>async { ... }</code> computation expression syntax.

### [AsyncBuilder.Zero](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncbuilder.html#Zero)

AsyncBuilder.Zero 
Zero 
Creates an asynchronous computation that just returns <code>()</code>. 
A cancellation check is performed when the computation is executed.

 The existence of this method permits the use of empty <code>else</code> branches in the 
 <code>async { ... }</code> computation expression syntax.

### [AsyncReplyChannel<'Reply>](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpasyncreplychannel-1.html)

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg> 
A message-processing agent which executes an asynchronous computation. 
The agent encapsulates a message queue that supports multiple-writers and
 a single reader agent. Writers send messages to the agent by using the Post
 method and its variations.

 The agent may wait for messages using the Receive or TryReceive methods or
 scan through all available messages using the Scan or TryScan method. 
MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.``.ctor`` 
``.ctor`` 
MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.``.ctor`` 
``.ctor``

PostAndTryAsyncReply 
MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Receive 
Receive 
MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Scan 
Scan 
MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Start 
Start

StartImmediate 
MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.TryPostAndReply 
TryPostAndReply 
MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.TryReceive 
TryReceive 
MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.TryScan 
TryScan

Error

DefaultTimeout 
MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.CurrentQueueLength 
CurrentQueueLength

Creates an agent. The <code>body</code> function is used to generate the asynchronous
 computation executed by the agent. This function is not executed until

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Post](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#Post)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Post 
Post 
Posts a message to the message queue of the MailboxProcessor, asynchronously.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.PostAndAsyncReply](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#PostAndAsyncReply)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.PostAndAsyncReply 
PostAndAsyncReply 
Posts a message to an agent and await a reply on the channel, asynchronously. 
The message is generated by applying <code>buildMessage</code> to a new reply channel
 to be incorporated into the message. The receiving agent must process this
 message and invoke the Reply method on this reply channel precisely once.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.PostAndReply](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#PostAndReply)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.PostAndReply 
PostAndReply 
Posts a message to an agent and await a reply on the channel, synchronously. 
The message is generated by applying <code>buildMessage</code> to a new reply channel
 to be incorporated into the message. The receiving agent must process this
 message and invoke the Reply method on this reply channel precisely once.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.PostAndTryAsyncReply](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#PostAndTryAsyncReply)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.PostAndTryAsyncReply 
PostAndTryAsyncReply 
Like AsyncPostAndReply, but returns None if no reply within the timeout period.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Receive](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#Receive)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Receive 
Receive 
Waits for a message. This will consume the first message in arrival order. 
This method is for use within the body of the agent.

 This method is for use within the body of the agent. For each agent, at most
 one concurrent reader may be active, so no more than one concurrent call to
 Receive, TryReceive, Scan and/or TryScan may be active.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Scan](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#Scan)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Scan 
Scan 
Scans for a message by looking through messages in arrival order until <code>scanner</code>
 returns a Some value. Other messages remain in the queue. 
Returns None if a timeout is given and the timeout is exceeded.

 This method is for use within the body of the agent. For each agent, at most
 one concurrent reader may be active, so no more than one concurrent call to
 Receive, TryReceive, Scan and/or TryScan may be active.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Start](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#Start)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Start 
Start 
Starts the agent.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.StartImmediate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#StartImmediate)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.StartImmediate 
StartImmediate 
Starts the agent immediately on the current operating system thread.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.TryPostAndReply](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#TryPostAndReply)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.TryPostAndReply 
TryPostAndReply 
Like PostAndReply, but returns None if no reply within the timeout period.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.TryReceive](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#TryReceive)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.TryReceive 
TryReceive 
Waits for a message. This will consume the first message in arrival order. 
This method is for use within the body of the agent.

 Returns None if a timeout is given and the timeout is exceeded.

 This method is for use within the body of the agent. For each agent, at most
 one concurrent reader may be active, so no more than one concurrent call to
 Receive, TryReceive, Scan and/or TryScan may be active.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.TryScan](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#TryScan)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.TryScan 
TryScan 
Scans for a message by looking through messages in arrival order until <code>scanner</code>
 returns a Some value. Other messages remain in the queue. 
This method is for use within the body of the agent. For each agent, at most
 one concurrent reader may be active, so no more than one concurrent call to
 Receive, TryReceive, Scan and/or TryScan may be active.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Error](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#Error)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Error 
Error 
Occurs when the execution of the agent results in an exception.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.DefaultTimeout](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#DefaultTimeout)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.DefaultTimeout 
DefaultTimeout 
Raises a timeout exception if a message not received in this amount of time. By default
 no timeout is used.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.CurrentQueueLength](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#CurrentQueueLength)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.CurrentQueueLength 
CurrentQueueLength 
Returns the number of unprocessed messages in the message queue of the agent.

### [MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Start](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-control-fsharpmailboxprocessor-1.html#Start)

MailboxProcessor<'Msg>.Start 
Start 
Creates and starts an agent. The <code>body</code> function is used to generate the asynchronous
 computation executed by the agent.

### [ExtraTopLevelOperators.single](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-extratopleveloperators.html#single)

ExtraTopLevelOperators.single 
single 
Converts the argument to 32-bit float. 
This is a direct conversion for all 
 primitive numeric types. For strings, the input is converted using <code>Single.Parse()</code>  with InvariantCulture settings. Otherwise the operation requires and invokes a <code>ToSingle</code> method on the input type.

### [ExtraTopLevelOperators.double](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-extratopleveloperators.html#double)

ExtraTopLevelOperators.double 
double 
Converts the argument to 64-bit float. 
This is a direct conversion for all 
 primitive numeric types. For strings, the input is converted using <code>Double.Parse()</code>  with InvariantCulture settings. Otherwise the operation requires and invokes a <code>ToDouble</code> method on the input type.

### [ExtraTopLevelOperators.uint8](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-extratopleveloperators.html#uint8)

ExtraTopLevelOperators.uint8 
uint8 
Converts the argument to byte. 
This is a direct conversion for all 
 primitive numeric types. For strings, the input is converted using <code>Byte.Parse()</code> on strings and otherwise requires a <code>ToByte</code> method on the input type.

### [ExtraTopLevelOperators.int8](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-extratopleveloperators.html#int8)

ExtraTopLevelOperators.int8 
int8 
Converts the argument to signed byte. 
This is a direct conversion for all 
 primitive numeric types. For strings, the input is converted using <code>SByte.Parse()</code>  with InvariantCulture settings.
 Otherwise the operation requires and invokes a <code>ToSByte</code> method on the input type.

### [ExtraTopLevelOperators.dict](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-extratopleveloperators.html#dict)

ExtraTopLevelOperators.dict 
dict 
Builds a read-only lookup table from a sequence of key/value pairs. The key objects are indexed using generic hashing and equality.

ExtraTopLevelOperators.readOnlyDict 
readOnlyDict 
Builds a read-only lookup table from a sequence of key/value pairs. The key objects are indexed using generic hashing and equality.

### [LanguagePrimitives.GenericEqualityComparer](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-languageprimitives.html#GenericEqualityComparer)

LanguagePrimitives.GenericEqualityComparer 
GenericEqualityComparer 
<pre>Return an F# comparer object suitable for hashing and equality. This hashing behaviour
 of the returned comparer is not limited by an overall node count when hashing F#
 records, lists and union types.</pre>

### [LanguagePrimitives.GenericEqualityERComparer](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-languageprimitives.html#GenericEqualityERComparer)

LanguagePrimitives.GenericEqualityERComparer 
GenericEqualityERComparer 
<pre>Return an F# comparer object suitable for hashing and equality. This hashing behaviour
 of the returned comparer is not limited by an overall node count when hashing F#
 records, lists and union types. This equality comparer has equivalence 
 relation semantics ([nan] = [nan]).</pre>

defaultIfNull

### [Operators.hash](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#hash)

Operators.hash 
hash 
A generic hash function, designed to return equal hash values for items that are 
 equal according to the "=" operator. By default it will use structural hashing
 for F# union, record and tuple types, hashing the complete contents of the 
 type. The exact behaviour of the function can be adjusted on a 
 type-by-type basis by implementing GetHashCode for each type.

### [Operators.limitedHash](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#limitedHash)

Operators.limitedHash 
limitedHash 
A generic hash function. This function has the same behaviour as 'hash', 
 however the default structural hashing for F# union, record and tuple 
 types stops when the given limit of nodes is reached. The exact behaviour of 
 the function can be adjusted on a type-by-type basis by implementing 
 GetHashCode for each type.

### [Operators.byte](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#byte)

Operators.byte 
byte 
Converts the argument to byte. This is a direct conversion for all 
 primitive numeric types. For strings, the input is converted using <code>Byte.Parse()</code> 
 with InvariantCulture settings. Otherwise the operation requires an appropriate
 static conversion method on the input type.

### [Operators.sbyte](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#sbyte)

 primitive numeric types. For strings, the input is converted using <code>SByte.Parse()</code>  
 with InvariantCulture settings. Otherwise the operation requires an appropriate
 static conversion method on the input type.

### [Operators.string](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#string)

Operators.string 
string 
Converts the argument to a string using <code>ToString</code>. 
For standard integer and floating point values and any type that implements <code>IFormattable</code>,
 <code>ToString</code> conversion uses <code>CultureInfo.InvariantCulture</code>.

### [Operators.decimal](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#decimal)

decimal

 primitive numeric types. For strings, the input is converted using <code>UInt64.Parse()</code>  
 with InvariantCulture settings. Otherwise the operation requires an appropriate
 static conversion method on the input type.

### [Operators.char](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#char)

Operators.char 
char 
Converts the argument to character. Numeric inputs are converted according to the UTF-16 
 encoding for characters. String inputs must be exactly one character long. For other
 input types the operation requires an appropriate static conversion method on the input type.

### [Operators.(|NonNullQuickV|)](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#(|NonNullQuickV|))

Operators.(|NonNullQuickV|) 
(|NonNullQuickV|) 
When used in a pattern checks the given value is not null. 
In a future revision of nullness support this may be unified with 'NonNullQuick'.

Operators.(|KeyValue|) 
(|KeyValue|) 
An active pattern to match values of type <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.keyvaluepair">KeyValuePair</a>

### [Checked.byte](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators-checked.html#byte)

Checked.byte 
byte 
Converts the argument to <code>byte</code>. This is a direct, checked conversion for all 
 primitive numeric types. For strings, the input is converted using <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.byte.parse">Byte.Parse</a> 
 with InvariantCulture settings. Otherwise the operation requires an appropriate
 static conversion method on the input type.

### [Checked.sbyte](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators-checked.html#sbyte)

Checked.sbyte 
sbyte 
Converts the argument to <code>sbyte</code>. This is a direct, checked conversion for all 
 primitive numeric types. For strings, the input is converted using <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.sbyte.parse">SByte.Parse</a> 
 with InvariantCulture settings. Otherwise the operation requires an appropriate
 static conversion method on the input type.

### [Checked.char](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators-checked.html#char)

Checked.char 
char 
Converts the argument to <code>char</code>. Numeric inputs are converted using a checked 
 conversion according to the UTF-16 encoding for characters. String inputs must 
 be exactly one character long. For other input types the operation requires an 
 appropriate static conversion method on the input type.

### [Unchecked](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators-unchecked.html)

Unchecked 
This module contains basic operations which do not apply runtime and/or static checks 
Unchecked.unbox 
unbox 
Unchecked.defaultof 
defaultof 
Unchecked.compare 
compare 
Unchecked.equals 
equals 
Unchecked.hash 
hash 
Unchecked.nonNull 
nonNull 
Unchecked.withNull 
withNull 
Unchecked.(|NonNullQuick|) 
(|NonNullQuick|)

### [Unchecked.unbox](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators-unchecked.html#unbox)

Unchecked.unbox 
unbox 
Unboxes a strongly typed value. This is the inverse of <code>box</code>, unbox<t>(box<t> a) equals a.

### [Unchecked.defaultof](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators-unchecked.html#defaultof)

Unchecked.defaultof 
defaultof 
Generate a default value for any type. This is null for reference types, 
 For structs, this is struct value where all fields have the default value. 
 This function is unsafe in the sense that some F# values do not have proper <code>null</code> values.

### [Unchecked.compare](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators-unchecked.html#compare)

Unchecked.compare 
compare 
Perform generic comparison on two values where the type of the values is not
 statically required to have the 'comparison' constraint.

### [Unchecked.equals](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators-unchecked.html#equals)

Unchecked.equals 
equals 
Perform generic equality on two values where the type of the values is not
 statically required to satisfy the 'equality' constraint.

### [Unchecked.hash](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators-unchecked.html#hash)

Unchecked.hash 
hash 
Perform generic hashing on a value where the type of the value is not
 statically required to satisfy the 'equality' constraint.

### [Unchecked.nonNull](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators-unchecked.html#nonNull)

Unchecked.nonNull 
nonNull 
Unsafely retypes the value from ('T | null) to 'T without doing any null check at runtime. This is an unsafe operation.

### [Unchecked.withNull](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators-unchecked.html#withNull)

Unchecked.withNull 
withNull 
Unsafely retypes the value from 'T to ('T | null), bypassing the 'not null' and 'not struct' constraints that F# otherwise requires in order to write ('T | null). This is an unsafe operation. 
This exists purely for interoperability with C# APIs that expose an unconstrained nullable generic, such as a method <code>T? M<T>()</code> or an interface member <code>T? GetValue<T>(int index)</code> where <code>T</code> has no <code>class</code> constraint and can therefore also be a struct. Without it such a signature cannot be implemented or consumed from F# without spurious FS3261 nullness warnings.

 It is unsafe precisely because it sidesteps those constraints. Unlike <a href="https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators.html#withNull">Operators.withNull</a> it adds no <code>not null</code> or <code>not struct</code> constraint, so the resulting ('T | null) can be formed even when <code>'T</code> is a struct, where <code>null</code> is not a representable value: there the annotation carries no runtime meaning and is erased, and assigning <code>null</code> to such a location yields <code>Unchecked.defaultof<'T></code> rather than a true null. Use it only to satisfy an interop signature.

### [Unchecked.(|NonNullQuick|)](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-operators-unchecked.html#(|NonNullQuick|))

Unchecked.(|NonNullQuick|) 
(|NonNullQuick|) 
When used in a pattern forgets 'nullness' of the value without any runtime check. This is an unsafe operation, as null check is being skipped and null value can be returned.

### [OptimizedClosures](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optimizedclosures.html)

### [Option.isSome](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#isSome)

Option.isSome 
isSome 
Returns true if the option is not None.

### [Option.isNone](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#isNone)

Option.isNone 
isNone 
Returns true if the option is None.

### [Option.defaultValue](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#defaultValue)

Option.defaultValue 
defaultValue 
Gets the value of the option if the option is <code>Some</code>, otherwise returns the specified default value. 
Identical to the built-in <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/defaultarg">defaultArg</a> operator, except with the arguments swapped.

### [Option.defaultWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#defaultWith)

Option.defaultWith 
defaultWith 
Gets the value of the option if the option is <code>Some</code>, otherwise evaluates <span class="fsdocs-param-name">defThunk</span> and returns the result. 
<span class="fsdocs-param-name">defThunk</span> is not evaluated unless <span class="fsdocs-param-name">option</span> is <code>None</code>.

### [Option.orElse](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#orElse)

Option.orElse 
orElse 
Returns <span class="fsdocs-param-name">option</span> if it is <code>Some</code>, otherwise returns <span class="fsdocs-param-name">ifNone</span>.

### [Option.orElseWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#orElseWith)

Option.orElseWith 
orElseWith 
Returns <span class="fsdocs-param-name">option</span> if it is <code>Some</code>, otherwise evaluates <span class="fsdocs-param-name">ifNoneThunk</span> and returns the result. 
<span class="fsdocs-param-name">ifNoneThunk</span> is not evaluated unless <span class="fsdocs-param-name">option</span> is <code>None</code>.

### [Option.get](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#get)

Option.get 
get 
Gets the value associated with the option.

### [Option.count](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#count)

Option.count 
count 
<code>count inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with None -> 0 | Some _ -> 1</code>.

### [Option.fold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#fold)

Option.fold 
fold 
<code>fold f s inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with None -> s | Some x -> f s x</code>.

### [Option.foldBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#foldBack)

Option.foldBack 
foldBack 
<code>fold f inp s</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with None -> s | Some x -> f x s</code>.

### [Option.exists](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#exists)

Option.exists 
exists 
<code>exists p inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with None -> false | Some x -> p x</code>.

### [Option.forall](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#forall)

Option.forall 
forall 
<code>forall p inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with None -> true | Some x -> p x</code>.

### [Option.contains](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#contains)

Option.contains 
contains 
Evaluates to true if <span class="fsdocs-param-name">option</span> is <code>Some</code> and its value is equal to <span class="fsdocs-param-name">value</span>.

### [Option.iter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#iter)

Option.iter 
iter 
<code>iter f inp</code> executes <code>match inp with None -> () | Some x -> f x</code>.

### [Option.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#map)

Option.map 
map 
<code>map f inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with None -> None | Some x -> Some (f x)</code>.

### [Option.map2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#map2)

Option.map2 
map2 
<code>map f option1 option2</code> evaluates to <code>match option1, option2 with Some x, Some y -> Some (f x y) | _ -> None</code>.

### [Option.map3](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#map3)

Option.map3 
map3 
<code>map f option1 option2 option3</code> evaluates to <code>match option1, option2, option3 with Some x, Some y, Some z -> Some (f x y z) | _ -> None</code>.

### [Option.bind](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#bind)

Option.bind 
bind 
<code>bind f inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with None -> None | Some x -> f x</code>

### [Option.flatten](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#flatten)

Option.flatten 
flatten 
<code>flatten inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with None -> None | Some x -> x</code> 
<code>flatten</code> is equivalent to <code>bind id</code>.

### [Option.filter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#filter)

Option.filter 
filter 
<code>filter f inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with None -> None | Some x -> if f x then Some x else None</code>.

### [Option.toArray](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#toArray)

Option.toArray 
toArray 
Convert the option to an array of length 0 or 1.

### [Option.toList](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#toList)

Option.toList 
toList 
Convert the option to a list of length 0 or 1.

### [Option.toNullable](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#toNullable)

Option.toNullable 
toNullable 
Convert the option to a Nullable value.

### [Option.ofNullable](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#ofNullable)

Option.ofNullable 
ofNullable 
Convert a Nullable value to an option.

### [Option.ofObj](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#ofObj)

Option.ofObj 
ofObj 
Convert a potentially null value to an option.

### [Option.toObj](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#toObj)

Option.toObj 
toObj 
Convert an option to a potentially null value.

### [Option.ofValueOption](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#ofValueOption)

Option.ofValueOption 
ofValueOption 
Convert a value option to an option.

### [Option.toValueOption](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-optionmodule.html#toValueOption)

Option.toValueOption 
toValueOption 
Convert an option to a value option.

Extensible printf-style formatting for numbers and other datatypes 
Format specifications are strings with "%" markers indicating format
 placeholders. Format placeholders consist of <code>%[flags][width][.precision][type]</code>.

### [Printf.kbprintf](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-printfmodule.html#kbprintf)

Printf.kbprintf 
kbprintf 
bprintf, but call the given 'final' function to generate the result.

### [Printf.kprintf](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-printfmodule.html#kprintf)

Printf.kprintf 
kprintf 
printf, but call the given 'final' function to generate the result.
 For example, these let the printing force a flush after all output has
 been entered onto the channel, but not before.

### [Printf.ksprintf](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-printfmodule.html#ksprintf)

Printf.ksprintf 
ksprintf 
sprintf, but call the given 'final' function to generate the result.
 See <code>kprintf</code>.

### [Printf.failwithf](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-printfmodule.html#failwithf)

Printf.failwithf 
failwithf 
Print to a string buffer and raise an exception with the given
 result. Helper printers must return strings.

### [Result.defaultValue](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-resultmodule.html#defaultValue)

Result.defaultValue 
defaultValue

### [Result.defaultWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-resultmodule.html#defaultWith)

Result.defaultWith 
defaultWith 
Gets the value of the result if the result is <code>Ok</code>, otherwise evaluates <span class="fsdocs-param-name">defThunk</span> and returns the result. 
<span class="fsdocs-param-name">defThunk</span> is not evaluated unless <span class="fsdocs-param-name">result</span> is <code>Error</code>.

### [Result.count](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-resultmodule.html#count)

<code>count inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with Error _ -> 0 | Ok _ -> 1</code>.

### [Result.fold](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-resultmodule.html#fold)

Result.fold 
fold

### [Result.foldBack](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-resultmodule.html#foldBack)

Result.foldBack 
foldBack

Result.forall

Result.contains

### [String](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html)

String 
Functional programming operators for string processing.  Further string operations
 are available via the member functions on strings and other functionality in
  <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.string">System.String</a>
 and <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.text.regularexpressions">System.Text.RegularExpressions</a> types.
  
String.collect 
collect 
String.concat 
concat 
String.exists 
exists

forall

init 
String.iter 
iter 
String.iteri 
iteri

length 
String.map 
map 
String.mapi 
mapi 
String.replicate 
replicate

### [String.collect](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html#collect)

String.collect 
collect 
Builds a new string whose characters are the results of applying the function <code>mapping</code>
 to each of the characters of the input string and concatenating the resulting
 strings.

### [String.concat](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html#concat)

String.concat 
concat 
Returns a new string made by concatenating the given strings
 with separator <code>sep</code>, that is <code>a1 + sep + ... + sep + aN</code>.

### [String.exists](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html#exists)

String.exists 
exists 
Tests if any character of the string satisfies the given predicate.

### [String.filter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html#filter)

String.filter 
filter 
Builds a new string containing only the characters of the input string
 for which the given predicate returns "true". 
Returns an empty string if the input string is null

### [String.forall](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html#forall)

String.forall 
forall 
Tests if all characters in the string satisfy the given predicate.

### [String.init](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html#init)

String.init 
init 
Builds a new string whose characters are the results of applying the function <code>initializer</code>
 to each index from <code>0</code> to <code>count-1</code> and concatenating the resulting
 strings.

### [String.iter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html#iter)

String.iter 
iter 
Applies the function <code>action</code> to each character in the string.

### [String.iteri](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html#iteri)

String.iteri 
iteri 
Applies the function <code>action</code> to the index of each character in the string and the
 character itself.

### [String.length](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html#length)

String.length 
length 
Returns the length of the string.

### [String.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html#map)

String.map 
map 
Builds a new string whose characters are the results of applying the function <code>mapping</code>
 to each of the characters of the input string.

### [String.mapi](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html#mapi)

String.mapi 
mapi 
Builds a new string whose characters are the results of applying the function <code>mapping</code>
 to each character and index of the input string.

### [String.replicate](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-stringmodule.html#replicate)

String.replicate 
replicate 
Returns a string by concatenating <code>count</code> instances of <code>str</code>.

### [ValueOption.isNone](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-valueoption.html#isNone)

ValueOption.isNone 
isNone 
Returns true if the value option is ValueNone.

### [ValueOption.defaultValue](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-valueoption.html#defaultValue)

ValueOption.defaultValue 
defaultValue 
Gets the value of the value option if the option is <code>ValueSome</code>, otherwise returns the specified default value. 
Identical to the built-in <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/defaultarg">defaultArg</a> operator, except with the arguments swapped.

### [ValueOption.defaultWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-valueoption.html#defaultWith)

ValueOption.defaultWith 
defaultWith 
Gets the value of the voption if the voption is <code>ValueSome</code>, otherwise evaluates <span class="fsdocs-param-name">defThunk</span> and returns the result. 
<span class="fsdocs-param-name">defThunk</span> is not evaluated unless <span class="fsdocs-param-name">voption</span> is <code>ValueNone</code>.

### [ValueOption.orElse](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-valueoption.html#orElse)

ValueOption.orElse 
orElse 
Returns <span class="fsdocs-param-name">voption</span> if it is <code>Some</code>, otherwise returns <span class="fsdocs-param-name">ifNone</span>.

### [ValueOption.orElseWith](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-valueoption.html#orElseWith)

ValueOption.orElseWith 
orElseWith 
Returns <span class="fsdocs-param-name">voption</span> if it is <code>Some</code>, otherwise evaluates <span class="fsdocs-param-name">ifNoneThunk</span> and returns the result. 
<span class="fsdocs-param-name">ifNoneThunk</span> is not evaluated unless <span class="fsdocs-param-name">voption</span> is <code>ValueNone</code>.

### [ValueOption.get](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-valueoption.html#get)

ValueOption.get

ValueOption.count 
count 
<code>count inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with ValueNone -> 0 | ValueSome _ -> 1</code>.

ValueOption.fold 
fold 
<code>fold f s inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with ValueNone -> s | ValueSome x -> f s x</code>.

ValueOption.foldBack 
foldBack

ValueOption.iter

### [ValueOption.map](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-valueoption.html#map)

ValueOption.map 
map

### [ValueOption.map2](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-valueoption.html#map2)

ValueOption.map2 
map2 
<code>map f voption1 voption2</code> evaluates to <code>match voption1, voption2 with ValueSome x, ValueSome y -> ValueSome (f x y) | _ -> ValueNone</code>.

### [ValueOption.map3](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-valueoption.html#map3)

ValueOption.map3 
map3 
<code>map f voption1 voption2 voption3</code> evaluates to <code>match voption1, voption2, voption3 with ValueSome x, ValueSome y, ValueSome z -> ValueSome (f x y z) | _ -> ValueNone</code>.

### [ValueOption.bind](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-valueoption.html#bind)

ValueOption.bind 
bind 
<code>bind f inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with ValueNone -> ValueNone | ValueSome x -> f x</code>

### [ValueOption.flatten](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-valueoption.html#flatten)

ValueOption.flatten 
flatten 
<code>flatten inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with ValueNone -> ValueNone | ValueSome x -> x</code> 
<code>flatten</code> is equivalent to <code>bind id</code>.

### [ValueOption.filter](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-valueoption.html#filter)

ValueOption.filter 
filter 
<code>filter f inp</code> evaluates to <code>match inp with ValueNone -> ValueNone | ValueSome x -> if f x then ValueSome x else ValueNone</code>.

### [AutoOpenAttribute](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-autoopenattribute.html)

AutoOpenAttribute 
Indicates a construct is automatically opened when brought into scope through
 an assembly reference or then opening of the containing namespace or module. 
When applied to an assembly, this attribute must be given a string
 argument, and this indicates a valid module or namespace in that assembly. Source
 code files compiled with a reference to this assembly are processed in an environment
 where the given path is automatically opened.

 When applied to a type or module within an assembly, then the attribute must not be given any arguments, and
 the type or module is implicitly opened when its enclosing namespace or module is opened.
  
AutoOpenAttribute.``.ctor`` 
``.ctor`` 
AutoOpenAttribute.``.ctor`` 
``.ctor`` 
AutoOpenAttribute.Path 
Path

### [AutoOpenAttribute.``.ctor``](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-autoopenattribute.html#``.ctor``)

AutoOpenAttribute.``.ctor`` 
``.ctor`` 
Creates an attribute used to mark a namespace or module path to be 'automatically opened' when an assembly is referenced

### [AutoOpenAttribute.``.ctor``](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-autoopenattribute.html#``.ctor``)

AutoOpenAttribute.``.ctor`` 
``.ctor`` 
Creates an attribute used to mark a module as 'automatically opened' when the enclosing namespace is opened

### [AutoOpenAttribute.Path](https://fsharp.github.io/fsharp-core-docs/reference/fsharp-core-autoopenattribute.html#Path)

AutoOpenAttribute.Path 
Path 
<pre>Indicates the namespace or module to be automatically opened when an assembly is referenced
 or an enclosing module opened.</pre>
